Ryan was going to go forward. I didn't ask him but I imagine he'd be happy to get a lead but he's happy to make his own running too. He just got it exactly spot on really. He would have a lot of options, he could be an American Derby horse; I'd say he's improving and we always thought he was a high-enough class horse last year as a two-year-old but things just didn't fall for him, he's probably matured and he's just got stronger now as well - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.It's the way Trinity College has been ridden most of the time, he said he likes it that way. The day at Epsom we held on to him a little bit and he just hung down the camber. He's out of a very good mare and we're learning about him; he quickened up very well and had the race in safe-keeping at the two, smart colt. Big run in the French Derby, quick turnaround. His mother, she sort of came out of nowhere and got better as a three-year-old, obviously he's a Dubawi so they usually progress - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.race: Slane (Pro/Am) Flat Race
quotes.quote: Barry said normally good horses get you out of trouble. The horse Joyeux Machin was tracking didn't stop and then he was locked in a little bit and he said a couple of doors closed. He said he's a good horse to get him out of trouble and he put it to bed in 100 yards. He's built on his first run, I hope. He didn't stop in Leopardstown, he was just beaten by a very good horse on the day and they were miles clear of the third. Hopefully he seems to be decent. He wouldn't show you a savage amount at home but when he went away to gallop on grass he improved every time he went away. This fella is a very relaxed, very easy individual, nothing bothers him. We'll have a talk now with the owners. He'll get an entry at Cheltenham and we'll see where we go from there - Paul Nolan, trainer.

quotes.race: Graham, Pam & Jo Birthday Celebration Cumberland Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Val Dancer did quite well last season and has really strengthened and grown over the summer. He really wants cut in the ground and he could be a type for races like the Midlands Grand National - Mel Rowley, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's come out of the Welsh Grand National amazingly well. In fact, two days after it we were asked to take him to our local point-to-point at Chaddesley Corbett and all the jockeys thought he would be their ride in the men's open! The couple of days after a tough race is such a crucial time, but he's been absolutely bouncing and full of himself after some lovely days out in the field - he's blooming and in rude health. I think we'll be looking towards a run in February next and the Haydock Grand National Trial is possibly what we'd be aiming for, but we certainly won't be contemplating the Grand National. Apart from the fact he wouldn't get in off his current mark, it's too early in his career. It's something we might consider in the future if all things carry on going well, but absolutely not this year and probably not next season either. It's very easy in the heat of the moment to get overexcited, but we're realistic and it's about making the best of him. There are plenty of other lovely long-distance prizes to go for. 16-01-25

It didn't turn into the strongest-looking race around, we thought he's well handicapped and if he didn't win it'd only be because he isn't experienced enough. He's a grand horse and a nice chaser in the making. He's only a novice still and we've still got a long way to go before we can have any smart targets. He likes slower ground and probably wants three miles and a fence really. That could be next season's job - Charlie Longsdon, trainer.

runners.comment: Others appeal more, for all that getting back on drier ground will benefit
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Cartmel (2m6f maiden; 11-4 joint-favourite) last May but not a lot since and others appeal more, for all that getting back on drier ground will benefit.

runners.comment: Low-mileage 6yo who ran his best race yet on handicap debut at Southwell (2m4f)
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 6yo who ran his best race yet on handicap debut at Southwell (2m4f, soft) and he's given the impression that this could be more his trip; respected.

runners.comment: Hard to make a solid case but this well-related 6yo could yet turn a corner
runners.spotlight: Hard to make a solid case but the ground was soft when pulled up on his handicap debut at Doncaster where he was upped to 3m from 2m; also has questions to answer on this drier ground but this well-related 6yo could yet turn a corner.

stable_tour.quote: A nice type who will probably run in a couple of bumpers this season. He's still a bit of a frame, so we won't rush him, but he's showing us some nice things at home. 06-11-24

prev_owners.owner: Nicolas Longere & Ecurie Haras Des Beaux

runners.comment: Refused over fences last time; a maiden over hurdles but has the form to feature
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden over hurdles but has placed form and he won six on the Flat; made a bright start over fences in January but didn't fancy it at Huntingdon and refused early; the cheekpieces are off but wouldn't be a surprise to see him run well.

runners.comment: Has only had seven races under rules and was a 3l winner last time at Ludlow
runners.spotlight: A 3l winner at Ludlow (2m5f, good to soft) to get off the mark over hurdles and he'd performed to a similar level before; up 6lb but Harry Atkins claims 7lb (3lb claimer employed last time) and this 6yo has only had seven races under rules.

runners.owner: Mrs J A Benson & Miss S N Benson
runners.comment: May be seen in a better light on this switch to handicaps and he's unraced beyond 2m4f
runners.spotlight: May be seen in a better light on this switch to handicaps and he's unraced beyond 2m4f (third in a 3m point), but wouldn't be the percentage play.

runners.breeder: E A R L Ecurie Des Mottes
runners.comment: Form figures confirm his current wellbeing but improvement has come on slow ground
runners.spotlight: Won two of his first three for this trainer but turned over at odds-on the last twice; only 1l higher than when beaten 2l last week at Fontwell (2m5f) but his improvement has come on slow ground; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

runners.owner: Rocket & Stan, Coxon, Hadfield And Stott
runners.comment: Headgear is added for this first handicap; trainers are respected
runners.spotlight: Has offered precious little in his qualifying races (2m-2m4f; 40-1 to 80-1) but he was second in an Irish point and headgear is added for this first handicap; trainers are respected (also run Mooserwirt), so needs a market check over this longer trip.

runners.comment: Plenty of risks involved after his long absence with a hood now fitted
runners.spotlight: Failed to build on a mildly encouraging hurdle debut and his first handicap was over fences when tailed off at Ludlow (2m4f) in late 2024; plenty of risks involved after his long absence with a hood now fitted.

prev_owners.owner: The Boundary Stables Partnership ( C R Barber)

runners.comment: Modest chase efforts last twice; no worthwhile form in handicaps over hurdles
runners.spotlight: No worthwhile form in his handicaps over hurdles and last two chase runs were also underwhelming.

racecards.verdict: After taking a step forward on his handicap debut and with probably more to offer over this far, MOOSERWIRT (nap) gets the vote.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Kastellion, 7/2 An Buachaill Rua, 4/1 Junior Des Mottes, 7/1 Mooserwirt, 8/1 Diamand De Vindecy, 10/1 Greedy Smith,  Thereyare, 20/1 Jo Arengeot Bey AA, 25/1 Maggies Boy,  Dublin City,  Rockvale

racecards.race_name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Definite chance on his penultimate run; however, not the only front-runner in the field
runners.spotlight: Ran no race at Windsor in January; however, prior to that he went close in a Class 2 handicap at Sandown (2m, soft; effective on good to soft); on a handy mark if factoring in Harry Atkins' claim; front runner, and not the only one.

quotes.race: Seat Unique Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's great for Tristan and he gets on well with this horse. Knickerbockerglory has always promised to do well and he loves soft and heavy ground. We'll keep running in these handicaps over hurdles and hopefully he can have more success on this sort of ground - Tom Messenger, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse who seems to have been around for ages. He holds his form well, loves soft ground and bolted up first time last season at Sandown when he finally got his conditions. It looks like we'll have to be patient again this season but he'll be ready when the rain comes. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Won easily last time and has shown that he can cope with this 3lb higher mark
runners.spotlight: Goes well at Taunton where he won comfortably a month ago (2m, heavy; second run in cheekpieces), and has shown he can deal with this 3lb higher mark and this sort of ground; has won going left-handed and, with a strike-rate of 6-18 over hurdles, this 9yo is likable.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I think they went too quickly, but I'm very pleased. Aurigny Mill looked the part - Robert Walford, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Boost Your Odds On Racing Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I've always thought Aurigny Mill was up at this level. This is the second run of his career that we have had a problem-free run up to. He had bruised feet all last season between every run, but we have got on top of all that. My son's partner rides him out most days and she said he was as good as ever, and she has got it right. Sean Bowen finished fourth on him in a bumper, and he said he would win loads of races, but he was backwards, and it took him time to get his breathing right. Fergus (Gillard) said he was off the bridle down the back straight, but he is settling now. He only had the hood on to help him settle. He is just a lovely horse - Victor Dartnall, trainer.

runners.comment: Won this last year before following up at Ayr and is well handicapped on all that
runners.spotlight: Won this last year before following up at Ayr and is well handicapped on all that; however, this season's wins have been over fences and it's been a struggle back hurdling the last twice.

quotes.race: Coral Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Four Sixes has an unbelievable constitution. He puts a lot into it and he probably won't run again this season - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's very tough and I'm keen to get him out over fences again. I think if he gets his jumping together he could be a really nice chaser from two and a half to three miles. He won at Ayr on good to soft ground, but I think he's better in softer conditions. He's got plenty of ability. 23-10-25

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras De La Croix Sonnet
runners.comment: Useful front-running chaser and could be interesting off his lower hurdle mark
runners.spotlight: Ended last year in excellent form over fences, with latest fourth coming behind the seriously progressive Thistle Ask; whereas he's 5-18 in that discipline and only 1-13 over hurdles, he's probably a better horse now than when last seen in this discipline; 5lb lower than his chase mark; front runs.

quotes.race: Brian And Sheila Vaughan Memorial Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Magistrato likes to do his own thing out in front and that's the first time I've sat on him. He was enthusiastic and his jumping was very good. I don't think we went all that quick and, once we got into a lovely rhythm, every time he heard another horse he kept pushing. Debbie [Cole] and her team said he's as fit as he's ever been and in good form - she wasn't half right - jockey Ben Jones, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Champion Hats Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Magistrato is a big baby and there's a lot to look forward to. We could go for a decent race and there's the Wensleydale at Wetherby, but I wouldn't run him if the ground was quick. There's also a juvenile at the Paddy Power meeting at Cheltenham - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: An ex-French horse who has not been easy, as he's been hard to settle. He was keen to get on with things when making a winning debut for us at Chepstow in October, and then disappointed when we stepped him up into Graded company on his next two starts. Soft ground didn't suit him and he probably wants a decent surface. All the time he was still a bit too keen and I think it may have been his breathing that was troubling him, so he's had an op in the summer. Slightly disappointing on his return on Saturday; probably wants stepping up to 2m4f now and we might keep him to the west-country tracks for the time being. 31-10-22

runners.breeder: Mme Marie Merienne , Mr Julien Merienne
runners.comment: A willing partner when winning at Haydock; up 5lb but not exposed over this far
runners.spotlight: It was a Class 4 he won at Haydock (good to soft; raced prominently) but that was his first time over this far since arriving from France and he's a willing partner; Charlie Maggs rides again off a 5lb higher mark.

quotes.race: Safer Gambling At CopyBet Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We've turned up on a lot of big days and Static is a good, hardy horse who wears his heart on his sleeve. He's not very big and was carrying a big weight in a lesser race, but I've always thought Haydock would suit him - Donald McCain, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Bought before the Cheltenham Festival, he ran a hell of a race in the Fred Winter. Then it was probably one run too many at Ayr. He was running well on his comeback at Chepstow - he just overraced a bit - and he had a really heavy fall. He was lucky to come out of it, but he's cantering again now and he's fine. We've always thought he'll be ideal for those handicap hurdles at Musselburgh. We might drop him in and get him to relax. 30-10-25

runners.comment: Well handicapped; back from a break and hasn't had many chances over this sort of trip
runners.spotlight: Hasn't fired as he can this season but he's well handicapped on form that wasn't that long ago; back from a break and hasn't had many chances over this sort of trip.

quotes.race: Kev And The Cheltenham Boys Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were keen to get another win into Norman Fletcher and he could end up a Lanzarote horse. He's very versatile ground wise so likes this and also heavy  He was still very green when he was in front - Willy Twiston-Davies, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Boylesports Money Back 2nd Meeting Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I swore a lot after Huntingdon as out of our novice hurdlers Norman Fletcher was the one who took to it best and I was amazed he jumped as poorly as he did there and fell. He's come a long way and is getting quicker, he's very correct at an obstacle. He wants nice ground and two-mile handicap hurdling, you wouldn't see it today but he's got a lot of pace - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

runners.comment: Ran his usual honest race when going down narrowly at Hereford in January
runners.spotlight: Just the one blip in five runs since joining Henry Oliver and ran his usual honest race when going down narrowly at Hereford in January (2m, soft; effective on drier); the winner of that race has failed to frank the form but this 7yo could still be in the thick of it here.

runners.breeder: Haras Du Hoguenet & Mr Gilles Le Baron
runners.comment: Novice win has worked out well and he wasn't far away on his handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Point/bumper winner; the form of his novice win at Catterick has worked out well (2m3f, good) and he wasn't beaten far on his handicap debut at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) despite a late mistake; how significant it is that Harry Atkins (aboard for both those runs; can do this weight) switches to Knickerbockerglory remains to be seen; respected nevertheless.

racecards.verdict: Not one of the field can be dismissed with confidence but IN THE AGE has a progressive profile and a handy weight to boot.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 In The Age, 3/1 Static, 9/2 Aurigny Mill, 5/1 The Four Sixes, 6/1 Norman Fletcher, 7/1 Knickerbockerglory, 20/1 Magistrato

racecards.race_name: Overton Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Placed in handicap hurdles and gets in off a lower mark for this debut over fences
runners.spotlight: Only won a maiden over hurdles but was placed in two handicaps and gets in off a lower mark for this debut over fences (second in his only point); worth considering.

stable_tour.quote: He won last year and then we took a couple of chances which didn't work out. He's a happier, stronger horse now and his first run back was really pleasing. With that under his belt he could be interesting next time. 30-10-25

runners.comment: Has got closer in each of her three runs over fences, last time beaten 5.5l at Warwick
runners.spotlight: Winning hurdler; has got closer in each of her three runs over fences, last time beaten 5.5l at Warwick (2m, good to soft); could well have more to offer.

stable_tour.quote: She was a bit in and out last season but she's going well at the moment and I hope she can add to her win at Kempton. She'll start back over hurdles but will go over fences at some stage. Hopefully she's more consistent with another year on her back. 22-10-25

runners.comment: He was too free last time at Southwell and now goes in cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Two seconds and a third over fences for this yard, from 2m to 2m4f; had a couple of blips as well but he was too free last time at Southwell and now goes in cheekpieces (tongue tied last time); possibilities.

stable_tour.quote: He came from Philip Hobbs and Johnston White and made a very promising start over fences last week when staying on really well. He's been keen in the past, so we had to ride him like that. He's a lovely big type who'll take a lot of beating next time. 20-11-25

He didn't look great the last time he ran but seems a lot better now. He'll go to Bangor on Saturday week and hopefully he'll come good. He isn't the easiest as he's quite keen-going. He should have won at Musselburgh in December when he just got done on the line and we're hopeful he can win before the end of the season. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Beaten when falling here last month but ran well for a good way
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Catterick in January (1m7f, soft), his third start after a long absence; beaten when falling here last month but ran well for a good way; can win off this mark by the looks.

runners.comment: Won last month but his run 20 days ago was a reminder of his inconsistency
runners.spotlight: Won narrowly at Ffos Las last month (2m, heavy) but his tailed-off run back there 20 days ago was a reminder of his inconsistency; he's capable, and on this ground, but comes with risks.

racecards.verdict: A chance is taken on chasing debutant PADDYS POLICY, who was second in his only point and has been placed off higher hurdle marks.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Paddys Policy, 3/1 Disguisedlimit, 7/2 Dj Pete, 100/30 Epinephrine, 11/2 Jiair Madrik

racecards.race_name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Racecourse Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Could raise his game now handicapping, especially back on this sort of ground
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in a bumper (good to soft) and competitive when falling two out in a Uttoxeter maiden hurdle (2m, heavy); below that level since but did lose a shoe last time and could raise his game now handicapping, especially on this better ground.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in a bumper at Hexham in November when second behind Forthfactor. He was running well on his first start over hurdles at Uttoxeter but fell at the second-last. Stan Sheppard, who rode him, was absolutely convinced he was going to win but I'm less sure. He then ran poorly next time at Ffos Las, but I think he just got stuck in the mud. He's declared to run at Ludlow on Wednesday and we'll see how we go. He looks a nice sort and is my choice for a dark horse. 18-02-26

runners.owner: The Old Stag Racing Sy Partnership
runners.comment: Back up in trip and off a reduced mark, there's some cause for optimism
runners.spotlight: Arrives in no sort of form but he has been running over 2m and he's won over nearly 3m in the past; back up in trip and off a reduced mark, there's some cause for optimism.

prev_owners.owner: Mr & Mrs G Calder & P M Warren
S Dufresne, B Milpied & G Luyckx

runners.comment: Poor this season but won easily here only four starts back last April
runners.spotlight: Bang out of form in his last three races but only four starts back last April he won as he liked around here (good to soft) off 5lb higher; couldn't put a line through him.

runners.comment: Won in Ireland; two fair runs over hurdles for this yard before pulling up over fences
runners.spotlight: Won a handicap hurdle for Henry de Bromhead whom she left for £5,500; they were perfectly respectable runs over hurdles for this yard in the winter and her non-completion last time (after wind surgery) was over fences; couldn't dismiss.

runners.comment: Modest run last time but wasn't far away in his two previous runs
runners.spotlight: Modest run last time but wasn't far away in his two previous runs after a wind operation and there are races in him off this mark.

stable_tour.quote: He's out of a mare I trained who was fourth behind Quevega in the Mares' Hurdle at the 2014 Cheltenham Festival and he was fourth in a bumper last time. He's had niggly issues through the winter, but we need to learn more about him. He's young and green but works well, so we've got something to look forward to over hurdles next time. 20-03-24

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras De La Haie Neuve
runners.comment: Encouraging fourth at Ludlow latest and handicaps were always going to be more like it
runners.spotlight: Signs of progress when fourth behind a useful winner in a 2m Ludlow novice last month (2m, soft) and handicaps were always going to be more like it; respected.

runners.comment: Has been showing enough to believe he'll pay his way in handicaps; had wind surgery
runners.spotlight: All runs on good to soft or soft; third in a bumper and has been showing enough to believe he'll pay his way in handicaps, last time finishing just ahead of Titanium Ring at Ludlow; likely contender after wind surgery.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse who is among our best novices. The form of his bumper was quite good. If he was to do what we think he can and win a novice hurdle or two, then he might end up in something like the Formby at Aintree on Boxing Day. 20-11-25
We really like him. He's had wind issues and hasn't had a smooth season, but he looks fantastic. He's ready to go handicapping on a pretty good mark. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Couldn't make a compelling case on this handicap debut and others preferred
runners.spotlight: Couldn't make a compelling case on this handicap debut and others preferred even if he is backed in the first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Perhaps flattered behind useful novices here last time as they went no pace
runners.spotlight: As at Carlisle on his reappearance, they were decent horses he chased home in a novice here last time, though likely he was flattered to be beaten 14l when they went no pace; should do better now into handicaps.

runners.comment: A lot more exposed than many in here but he's been in cracking form for a while now
runners.spotlight: A lot more exposed than many in here but he's been in cracking form since returning from an absence and his defeat at Leicester was no backward step (2m4f, good to soft); firmly in the mix.

racecards.verdict: Henry Daly's TITANIUM RING is a likely improver on his handicap debut, as are Fanny Moon (second choice) and Joeybottles.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Eric Carmen, 100/30 Joeybottles, 6/1 Titanium Ring, 7/1 Fanny Moon, 8/1 Golden Identity, 10/1 Supreme Yeats,  Love Me,  Ayyadieh, 14/1 Noble George, 20/1 Rock Hurley

racecards.race_name: BetWright Beeswing Mares' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Grade 2/Listed winner over hurdles; leading claims if seeing out this new trip
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 2 novice hurdle at Sandown (2m4f, soft) last February and scored at Exeter (2m1f, heavy) in December on second chase start; reverted to hurdles with all-the-way Listed win at Warwick (2m5f, heavy) last month; also effective on good/good to soft; half-sister to a 2m7f winner and there's every chance she'll stay this far; leading claims if seeing it out.

quotes.race: Get The Best Odds With Oddschecker Warwick Mares' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were slightly fortuitous because we were going to go to Exeter for the Listed novice chase there on Sunday, but luckily we were also entered here and when Exeter looked likely to be called off, we re-routed and came here. Hollygrove Cha Cha loves that ground and won the Jane Seymour at Sandown last year on very soft ground, she relishes it and stays very well. We went to Cheltenham last year for the mares' novices' hurdle and it didn't work. There are plenty of nice races outside of Cheltenham, so we'll just have a little think about where we go from here. Hurdles or fences, I don't think it matters. It didn't work at Windsor the last day over fences but she wasn't really experienced enough for a big handicap like that and found the track a little bit sharp and tight. She is a very good jumper and I think we'll swap and change between hurdles and fences depending on when the race comes up - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Cheltenham Festival Betting Guide Jane Seymour Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We've got some really nice young horses and Hollygrove Cha Cha is right up there. She's a pretty smart mare and she's a darling. She's won five of her six races and the only time she got beaten was at Taunton when she found the track a bit tight and quick, but she's not slow and I wouldn't be averse to dropping back in trip. She's in Mares' Hurdle and Mares' Novices' Hurdle at Cheltenham. It isn't guaranteed but it's quite tempting - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Best UK Bookie Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hollygrove Cha Cha is a really smart mare. We've brought her along steadily and she's done nothing but improve. She jumped well, just a couple of small errors but a lot better than Ludlow. The speed she showed from the back of the last under a penalty was pretty impressive. There's a Listed race at Taunton at the end of this month, and you've got the Jane Seymour. All being well, we'll plot a route towards Cheltenham in March if we can - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

quotes.race: Angela Hems Happy 65th Birthday Mares' "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hollygrove Cha Cha has got an engine. Her jumping has been good at home but it's been so dry we haven't been able to school on the grass as much as we'd like. She was still green and immature but she'll improve for it. I'll probably drop her back to two miles - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We'll put in lots of entries for her, one of which will be the Mares' Chase. We might look at the National Spirit at Fontwell and a three-mile Listed race at the end of this month, but she won really well at Warwick the other day and she jumped great back over hurdles. She's also been jumping fences well. She was third in the Colin Parker on her chasing debut, where if she'd jumped the last she probably would have won, but she just got in tight to that. She won at Exeter very impressively, but her Windsor run was a bit of a disappointment as she found the track a bit sharp in handicap company, and she didn't jump very well.  11-02-26

runners.owner: S T Racing - The Founders' Syndicate
runners.comment: Won 2m4f handicap at Windsor two runs ago; needs to settle at new trip, but not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Game when winning 2m4f handicap at Windsor (good) on New Year's Day, shaping as though she would be worth a crack at a staying trip; soundly beaten at Ascot (2m3f, good to soft) since, and in view of this longer distance it's a concern she failed to settle that day, but she's not ruled out.

quotes.race: Fitzdares New Year's Day Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Listentoyourheart last time and unfortunately the hurdles were out and that didn't really benefit her because her jumping's so good. With the two quick hurdles up the straight I knew it would benefit her today. She's genuine and we rode her a bit more forward today and that helped too. When the other horse came to her she picked up again. She's good and gutsy - Tristan Durrell, jockey.

quotes.race: Play Coral 'Racing-Super-Series' For Free Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Listentoyourheart was good there, she snipped through that gap. She's tough, she's hardy and has a little bit of experience under her belt. We got on with it and got some racing into her early in the season. Today was always going to be harder, but we were preparing her for it. When they turned the taps on, she took about five strides to pick up when the others picked up immediately in front of her. Some would back out of that hole, but she's not like that - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: CSP Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Two and a half miles will be no issue and Listentoyourheart actually ran well on softer ground at Aintree, but I'm not in a massive hurry to pitch her in. While the ground is like this we don't have to - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won at Windsor in a valuable race over this trip [2m4f], showing a gritty attitude in the process, but was on the front end a bit too strong at Ascot at the weekend. If she got into the Martin Pipe there's a chance she'd go, but we may wait for Aintree. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Two-time Listed winner who was Grade 3 runner-up last time; firmly in calculations
runners.spotlight: Two Listed novice hurdle wins last season (2m5f/3m, good/good to soft), one of them at Doncaster, and close second in Grade 3 at Punchestown (2m4f, soft) last month; this Irish challenger is firmly in calculations.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was all down to Jordan Gainford as he told me how to ride World Of Fortunes and that she'd stay. He has her to look forward to in the better races in the spring - Brian Hughes, jockey.

quotes.race: Cheesestrings Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
quotes.quote: World Of Fortunes is a lovely mare with loads of ability and is a nice one going forward. She can sharpen up a bit more - Jordan Gainford, rider.

runners.comment: Has made a good start for her new yard but has plenty to find in today's company
runners.spotlight: Won handicap at Carlisle (2m3f, soft) in December on stable debut and went close at Newcastle (2m4f, heavy) in January; could continue to progress for this yard but has plenty to find in today's company.

quotes.race: Ferry Ales Brewery Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Pitwood Road had already won a 10,000GBP bonus at Ayr so this is great and it's why we've been campaigning her in Britain. The bonus is fantastic for British owners and British-bred horses, so it's opened our eyes a bit. Derrick [Mossop] has been a great owner of mine for the last few years and he sends the younger horses to us so we can go to Britain and race. He left her with us this season and it's paid off, so hopefully she can stay - Terence O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won nicely on her debut for us in a 2m3½f handicap hurdle at Carlisle in mid-December off a mark of 105. She jumped well and enjoyed the soft ground. I liked the way she battled on strongly to the line and it'll be interesting to see how far she goes up the handicap ladder. 31-12-25

runners.comment: Two wins in autumn but progress has stalled since; going right-handed would be preferable
runners.spotlight: Kicked off current campaign with two handicap wins in a row in the autumn (2m3f/2m7f, good); her progress has stalled at Doncaster (3m, good/soft) on her last two starts and, while she may still have more to offer when returning to a right-handed track, she's once more going left-handed today.

runners.comment: Three-time course winner; drying conditions are a positive but she looks out of her depth
runners.spotlight: Three-time course winner for whom the drying conditions are a positive but she looks out of her depth this afternoon.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Go North Cab On Target Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I love racing because of the horses and Starlyte is the sort of horse I love. She's only tiny but she's so brave. You have to drop her in and let her pass horses and I'm delighted for the owners Allan and Anne Grant who've just got married - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Follow Thehawkponteland On Instagram Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Starlyte needs a fast-run two-and-a-half miles and she's the most game horse. It's her attitude that wins her races - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She came to us from the Flat and made a flying start by winning a 2m4½f Newcastle handicap hurdle. We'll keep her to that trip with a view to going up to 3m later. She desperately needs good ground and is ready to go as soon as things dry out. 25-01-23

runners.comment: Needs another step forward but things appear to have clicked for this lightly raced 7yo
runners.spotlight: Reappeared with good second to Rockola Vogue in Ascot handicap (2m7f, good) in November then went one better at Kempton (3m, good) in December; she needs another step forward now up in grade but things appear to have clicked for this lightly raced 7yo and she could be a contender.

stable_tour.quote: Another very smart mare. We were delighted to get her as we didn't think we'd be able to afford her at the sales in December. She won first time out at Fakenham in April, despite getting knocked sideways and the track being too sharp for her. She doesn't show much at home and you'll only see how good she is in the last half-mile of a race. She probably wouldn't have the size and scope of Metkayina or Jasmine Bliss, but she's a warrior. She'll start out next month and we don't know how good she can be, so the dream is alive. 24-10-24

runners.comment: Has run well in Listed/Grade 2 races this season and today's new trip may be within range
runners.spotlight: Won 2m4f handicap at Sandown (soft) in December and she ran well in defeat in Listed/Grade 2 races on next two starts (2m4f/1m7f, good/soft); mid-race unseat at Cheltenham last week; she's a half-sister to a 3m2f winner and it's possible this new trip will be within range; in with a chance.

stable_tour.quote: She won two novices last season and I was happy with her comeback at Exeter last Friday. She carried a lot of weight and there should be plenty more nice races for her this season. We could look at Sandown, Ascot and Cheltenham. 12-11-25

A lovely mare, she won an Aintree bumper before finishing fourth in a Listed one at Cheltenham in November. I'll probably give her one more run before the big mares' bumper at Aintree's Grand National meeting in April, but I'm relishing her as a novice hurdler next season. 18-01-24

runners.comment: She's won handicap on last four hurdle starts; remains to be seen where limitations lie
runners.spotlight: Highly progressive for new yard this season and has won handicaps on her last four hurdle starts (2m7f-3m1f, good-soft), most recently in comfortable fashion at Ludlow last month; this is a much tougher test of her credentials but it remains to be seen where her limitations now lie.

quotes.race: Choose Fibrus Broadband Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was a bit worried about stepping up in trip with Tankardstown Diva as she can be hard on herself but she's learning - Ian Donoghue, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for the thriving 7yo TANKARDSTOWN DIVA, who continued her handicap hurdle winning spree in fine style at Ludlow last month
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Hollygrove Cha Cha, 11/4 World Of Fortunes, 5/1 Listentoyourheart, 8/1 Sunset Marquesa, 9/1 Tankardstown Diva, 10/1 Star Walking, 12/1 Rockola Vogue, 33/1 Pitwood Road, 100/1 Starlyte

racecards.race_name: BetWright Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Final) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Made it 2-2 in handicaps when winning here last month; progressive and holds solid claims
runners.spotlight: Won maiden hurdle at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) in December on second rules start and 2-2 in handicaps since (2m5f/2m6f, good to soft/heavy), the latest here last month; progressive and holds solid claims.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a star. He seems to be improving all the time, he's very versatile and appears to go on any ground. He's qualified for the Cab On Target final at Kelso on Saturday week, which is a valuable race for a horse with his rating. He's also qualified for the Triple Crown final at Punchestown, so if he runs well at Kelso he could go there as well. 13-03-26

quotes.race: JTC Pizzalicious Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thank You Blue jumped really well. He'll probably be better over a little bit further, I was just forcing him for the last half a mile. He was good over the last two and galloped to the line - Sean Quinlan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: Like Constitution Hill he's a son of Blue Bresil and it's incredible how jumping issues came to the fore with this guy - not over hurdles but over fences. He fell twice and was pulled up three times over fences but he's done very well this season back over hurdles, winning his last three. He'll run again under a penalty this week - he has two entries at Ayr on Friday, one over fences and one over hurdles. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Two wins last year; respectable runs since; lightly raced and may still have more to offer
runners.spotlight: Won at Perth (2m4f, good to soft) last April and followed up at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in December; he's performed respectably here (2m6f, good to soft) and at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) since and this lightly raced 6yo may still have more to offer, especially now back up in trip.

quotes.race: Never Ordinary At bet365 Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Baratablet is a grand little horse, he's never done anything wrong. He's the same at home, he doesn't do anything flash, he just does what you want - Nicky Richards, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.It was Baratablet's first run of the season and we were going as quick as I could go. He's a horse who will get three miles so I knew when I set into him that he'd respond - Brian Hughes, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's named after the most popular sweetie in Scotland, that's how owner Jimmy Fyffe named him - they're too sweet for me! He's well named as he's a sweet horse who's done nothing wrong in his life - he's had three wins over hurdles now and has only been out of the first three once in seven runs. He ran at Kelso on Monday, finishing fourth behind Both Barrels. 31-12-25

runners.comment: Not beaten far back over hurdles in January and the step back up in trip could be a plus
runners.spotlight: Course maiden hurdle winner who was a promising second on handicap debut at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in November; not beaten far in fifth when back over hurdles at Haydock (1m7f, good to soft) in January and the step back up in trip could be a positive move; possible player.

stable_tour.quote: He joined us from Pauline Robson. He was second in a handicap hurdle at Ayr last week, when he gave a lot of weight away to the winner. He did most things right and he'll go chasing now. He has won a bumper and over hurdles, and was then fifth in a Grade 2 hurdle at Kelso. Trips between 2m and 2m5f will suit for now, as will a bit of cut in the ground. 19-11-25

runners.comment: Won at Sedgefield on first crack at 2m4f but tailed off at Catterick since
runners.spotlight: Enhanced his good record at Sedgefield when winning there in a first-time tongue-tie on Boxing Day on his first crack at 2m4f (good to soft); however, tailed off at Catterick since on soft ground he should have handled, and he needs to bounce back with a visor now added.

stable_tour.quote: His form over a trip on the Flat in France was good and he'll probably want further than 2m over hurdles in time. He was a very pleasing second in a novice hurdle at Sedgefield last week and looked to love the soft ground. I'm looking forward to him. 16-10-24

runners.comment: Won three times in the winter and bled from the nose when well beaten at Catterick latest
runners.spotlight: Yet to run well at Kelso (three attempts) and well beaten at Catterick last time; however, he had an excuse (bled from the nose) and he won three times in the winter (2m1f/2m3f, soft/good to soft); not written off.

quotes.race: Bowel Screening Programme Saves Lives Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We thought we were towards the top end when Bathgate won last time, but he's only improved again. A race that drags him into it for a bit longer will suit him better - Phil Kirby, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Has done well in cheekpieces, winning her last two; this thriving mare is respected
runners.spotlight: With a new yard this season and has been better than ever since these cheekpieces went on, winning here (2m2f, good to soft) in December and following up at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft); this thriving mare is respected.

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras Du Puy
runners.comment: In good form in cheekpieces of late and this three-time course winner might be thereabouts
runners.spotlight: These cheekpieces and a switch to prominent tactics have prompted good performances at Ayr (2m4f, soft) on his last two starts, finishing second then first; he's won three times here in the past (including on good to soft) and might be thereabouts.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Eloi Du Puy and the second dominated the race and he was very tough to dig deep after the last to get his head in front, which is great because he won four races two seasons ago. But last season was a blank for him - Nick Alexander, trainer.

quotes.race: Graeme Todd Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier) (Div I)
quotes.quote: I hope there will be lots more to come from Eloi Du Puy. He's backed up his win here last time and I'm still hoping we haven't got to the end of him yet. It was a very close finish, so he shouldn't go up much for that and should still be competitive. I know there are races for him at the next two meetings here and fingers crossed all being well we'll come back here for them - Nick Alexander, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a little setback and is out of training but he's due back in on December 1. The plan is to go chasing with him. He's still a young horse, so if the issue we had flares up again we won't hesitate to put him away for the season. He'll improve for going up to 3m and he jumps very well. I'd like to think he'll be a nice staying chaser. I couldn't believe he wasn't better sooner for us. The penny dropped last season when he stepped up in trip. I think the sire's stock improve for age and a trip. They're quite buzzy horses, so you tend to think they want 2m, but actually they don't come into their own until they go over further. 21-11-24

runners.owner: G R Orchard & Mrs J M Gray

prev_owners.owner: Arf Racing, Davide Satalia & Mme Michele Juhen-Cypres

runners.comment: Off a reduced mark he was third to Eloi Du Puy at Ayr and he might not be far away
runners.spotlight: His French win came in 2023 and he's 0-6 in Britain, but he's dropped down the weights and ran well when third to Eloi Du Puy at Ayr (2m4f, soft) last month; has also shown promise on good to soft; might not be far away.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a bit frustrating. He's not quite lived up to my expectations but I still believe in him. He's dropped down the ratings a little bit but I think he'll have his day in the sun. We'll keep plugging away with him in novice and handicap chases this season. He shaped as though I've been running him over the wrong distance when he finished third at Wincanton on Sunday and he'll now have options over marathon trips. 02-11-23

He's got more than enough ability to win off his mark but he's tricky and it's difficult to get his head in front. We've tried nearly everything and, as is always the case, there are plenty of ‘experts' telling us what we should do. We may try headgear in desperation one day but knowing him I'm not sure whether that would help or hinder him. He's a fun horse as he usually runs well but he's not fun for the trainer! 28-02-24

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.comment: He's tumbled down weights since British debut; not shaping as though about to capitalise
runners.spotlight: Won four in a row over hurdles in Ireland in May-July 2024; he's tumbled down the weights since his British debut in November 2025 but hasn't been shaping as though he's about to take advantage.

quotes.race: Waterford FC Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rauzan was behind the bridle the whole way, just struggling to hold his position. The trip was too short. Hugh said once he pulled him out wide he just locked onto it and once he met the rising ground he just went away from them - Eoin Doyle, trainer.

quotes.race: Dunlop Homes Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rauzan was in good nick, but the only problem was the drop back in trip. Slower ground out there helped and he handles it no problem - Hugh Morgan, rider.

quotes.race: Dunmore East Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rauzan wasn't really suited by Winter ground. His jumping has come together and I think there is a bit of improvement in him. He could do a job on the Flat over a trip - Eoin Doyle, rider

runners.comment: A win and a good third from his two handicaps; in excellent hands to continue to progress
runners.spotlight: Won on handicap debut at Wetherby (2m3f, soft) on Boxing Day before 4l third of 17 to Judicial Deference at Haydock (2m5f, good to soft) in January; he's 9lb better off with his old rival, who has won again since, and is in excellent hands to continue to progress; strong candidate.

stable_tour.quote: He was a little frustrating last year but ran better on his reappearance in a 2m maiden hurdle at Kelso. He was beaten far enough but he was running through the line in a way that suggested he was a stayer in the making. A step up in trip should suit him. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Pulled up at Ayr last time but on soft; two wins over C&D on good ground in the autumn
runners.spotlight: 11yo who was tailed off over C&D (good to soft) in November and pulled up at 100-1 at Ayr (2m4f, soft) last month on his sole start since; however, the drying conditions are a positive, with his last five wins coming on good ground, and he won two in a row over C&D last autumn to take his winning tally at Kelso to four; no surprise if he bounces back with a bold show.

quotes.race: Go North Sea Pigeon Series Final (A Handicap Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Navigator fell in this race last year and he never really recovered. I deliberately went to Sedgefield because I thought if there was anywhere he could get his confidence back it would be there, and he needed it. He's got a lot of ability, he's a big beautiful horse, he's stunning - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

runners.comment: Of interest on her autumn form but not quite at the same level in the winter
runners.spotlight: Won novice hurdle at Perth (2m4f, good) last September and good second off this mark there (2m4f, soft) next time; however, she wasn't quite at the same level in the winter and needs something extra now in cheekpieces.

runners.owner: Ursa Major Ltd, Dj Goodman & Partner
runners.comment: Encouraging fourth on handicap debut at Ayr and every chance he'll continue to progress
runners.spotlight: Good-ground point runner-up who has improved with each of his four runs under rules and was an encouraging fourth on handicap debut at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in January; there's every chance he'll continue to progress; chance.

runners.comment: Held at Haydock in January but in good form over hurdles previously; AW win last week
runners.spotlight: Won easily at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in November and runner-up to progressive winner at Catterick (2m3f, good) in December; soundly beaten behind Judicial Deference at Haydock (2m5f, good to soft) in January but he's probably better than that and he won on the AW last week; not ruled out.

racecards.verdict: The unexposed 6yo BROOKSIDE LA (nap) has made a good start to life in handicaps and is open to further improvement for Dan Skelton.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Judicial Deference, 9/2 Brookside La, 6/1 Speiriuil, 8/1 Baratablet,  Captain Butler, 9/1 Eloi Du Puy, 10/1 Jericoacoara,  Rock Dj, 16/1 Bathgate,  Wasthatok, 20/1 Kingston Narcissus,  Coconut Splash,  Mountain Molly, 40/1 Rauzan, 50/1 The Navigator

racecards.race_name: BetWright Herring Queen Series Final Mares' Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: Elevage Du Colombier, Haras De Saint-Voi
runners.comment: 2-time novice hurdle winner who is in top hands and could be better than her opening mark
runners.spotlight: Won two Grade 3 bumpers in France and she made it 2-5 in novice hurdles when scoring cosily at Market Rasen (2m, soft) last month; also effective on good ground; in top hands and could be better than her opening mark.

quotes.race: Support The Injured Jockeys Fund Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Mares' Nov' Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We were only hacking around. Khrisma was very professional, she's grown up so much in the last year or so and she's really come on for that race at Punchestown - Nico De Boinville, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I like her and she has had some solid AQPS Flat form in France. She needed to learn to settle last season but, amazingly for a horse who pulled so hard at home, she was great on the racecourse when she finished third at Windsor and second at Punchestown. She travelled into the race in Ireland like a good horse and got beaten by a hotpot. She's still a novice over hurdles and she's well educated. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Two wins from first three starts for this yard and perhaps her latest run came too soon
runners.spotlight: Two wins (1m7f/2m, good to soft/heavy) from her first three starts for this yard and perhaps her latest run at Newbury three weeks ago came too soon, just six days after she won at Fontwell; not discounted.

runners.comment: Won at Taunton last month and could continue to progress now switched to handicaps
runners.spotlight: Went close at Taunton (2m, good to soft) in January on second hurdle start and improved again to win there (2m, heavy) last month; could continue to progress now switched to handicaps and she's one to consider.

quotes.race: 9 March Dragonbet Festival Fever Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Beauty In The Park is improving all of the time. She's qualified for the Herring Queen Final at Kelso and that'll be a nice prize to aim at - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A well-bred mare, related to three winners, with bags of stamina in her pedigree. She showed promise in her two bumpers, although she wasn't your typical bumper horse, and is going to want a trip now she tackles mares' novice hurdles. Has done plenty of schooling and is ready to run as soon as we get more rain. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Respectable fifth in Grade 2 novice last month and not ruled out in her first handicap
runners.spotlight: One win from her six hurdle starts, which came at Wetherby (2m, soft) in November; performed respectably in fifth in Grade 2 novice at Kempton (2m, good to soft) last month and she's not ruled out in her first handicap.

runners.owner: Turf Club 2024 & The Burling Family Ltd
runners.comment: Clear second on h'cap debut at Ludlow; could play another leading role even now 4lb higher
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in two novice hurdles towards end of last year (2m/2m5f, good/good to soft) and filled the same position when beaten half a length on last month's handicap debut at Ludlow (2m, soft); she was well clear of the third last time and could play another leading role even now 4lb higher.

stable_tour.quote: She's a very nice mare, a half-sister to Willmount. She's more than capable as she placed in a couple of bumpers at Uttoxeter and Huntingdon, but she ran a shocker over hurdles at the latter track in February. She'll try again over hurdles this season. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Runner-up on h'cap hurdle debut at Carlisle; could still be capable of better in this code
runners.spotlight: Five-time Flat winner (including on good ground) who won at Hexham (2m, heavy) in December on second hurdle start; 6l second of 14 behind improving winner on handicap hurdle debut at Carlisle (2m1f, soft) last month and could still be capable of better in this code in view of her Flat form.

quotes.race: Download The Vickers.Bet App Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: We were disappointed when Azahara Palace got beat at Catterick, but I think the course caught her out. She's quite difficult to train, and was still learning here, but hopefully she'll keep progressing - Hughie Morrison, trainer, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: I don't think she's a miler and I think she'll get 1m4f now. She ran last time at Newbury behind Burrito but the ground was too firm. The winner is a Group horse and I thought beforehand he was the one we all had to beat. She's got races in her and, although she'll run on fast going, she basically needs the speed to be taken out of the ground for her to be at her most effective. She could even run up to a mark of 90 on the right surface. 29-05-25

runners.comment: Close second at Ludlow last month and on that evidence there's mileage in her opening mark
runners.spotlight: Point winner who has improved with each of her three hurdle runs, going close at Ludlow (2m, soft) last month; the winner has followed up in a handicap, suggesting there should be mileage in this mare's opening mark.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely mare, she's an Irish point-to-point winner who went straight over hurdles at Stratford, but she got it all wrong that day, ran way too keen in front and fell at the last. Luckily she's fine but we'll put things on hold a little bit, come back to two miles, and down the line I'm sure she's going to make a nice horse. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Runner-up to Beauty In The Park at Taunton and she's 6lb better off on this handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Fourth in warm novice hurdle against males at Newbury (2m, good to soft) in January and runner-up to Beauty In The Park at Taunton (2m, heavy) next time, beaten just over 3l; she's 6lb better off with the winner on this handicap debut and could have a part to play in a first-time tongue-tie.

runners.comment: Likeable performance when clear second at Wincanton; could be in the mix on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Point winner who has improved with each of her three hurdle runs, finishing clear of the rest when second at Wincanton (1m7f, good to soft) recently; that was a likeable effort and she could be in the mix on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Could benefit from the drop back in trip but others arrive with more compelling claims
runners.spotlight: Won two novice hurdles last May (2m/2m1f) and she could benefit from this drop back in trip; however, she hasn't shone in handicaps this winter and others are more compelling, including stablemate First Candidate.

stable_tour.quote: She won twice over hurdles for us earlier in the year but found the soft ground against her at Hexham on Friday and ran below par. We'll find some better ground for her through the winter and hopefully in the spring there'll be some nicer races for her. 10-11-25

runners.comment: 5l second of four on h'cap debut; it looked a warm little contest; may have more to offer
runners.spotlight: Two-time point runner-up (including on good to yielding) who has finished second on her last two starts, most recently on handicap debut at Exeter (2m, heavy); she was beaten 5l in that four-runner race last time but it looked a warm little contest and she may have more to offer.

runners.comment: Easy win in recent Catterick maiden and she could be progressive; not discounted
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner (good to soft) who had been headed but was disputing second when falling two out at Wincanton (2m4f, soft) in December on her sole handicap start; she's since easily won a maiden at Catterick (1m7f, good) and she could be progressive; not discounted.

stable_tour.quote: She won a bumper at Sedgefield on her debut but took quite a keen hold on her next two runs at Cheltenham. She was second on her comeback over hurdles at Chepstow, which was a good run, and I don't think it was her true running last time at Hereford. She should be able to make her mark in the mares' novice hurdle division. 18-11-25

runners.breeder: Mill House Stud & Mr N Farrell
runners.owner: Mrs S Lee And E Lee
runners.comment: Makes handicap debut off workable mark after wind op; represents in-form southern stable
runners.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who has run well in defeat on two of her three hurdle starts, most recently runner-up at Catterick (1m7f, good) in December; has had wind op since; makes handicap debut off workable mark and she's the sole runner here today for her in-form southern trainer; interesting.

runners.comment: Runner-up on first two hurdle starts before Hereford blip; she's not ruled out each-way
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner who was runner-up on her first two hurdle starts (2m/2m1f, soft/good to soft); disappointing favourite at Hereford (2m, soft) since but she failed to settle and was hampered a couple of times; retains potential and she's not ruled out each-way on handicap debut.

racecards.verdict: Topweight KHRISMA beat a quality field in a novice at Market Rasen last month to post her second hurdle win and can follow up.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/8 Khrisma, 8/1 First Candidate, 10/1 Beauty In The Park,  Our Peggy, 12/1 Queenie St Clair,  Belle Le Grand, 14/1 Diamonds Galore,  Yeld To Call, 16/1 Anariza,  Azahara Palace,  Riviera Walk,  Crystal Days, 33/1 Changemyluck,  Klassy Pearl,  Madame La Papillon, 40/1 Gintime

racecards.race_name: BetWright Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Series Final) (GBB Race)

prev_owners.owner: The Boundary Stables Partnership ( C R Barber)

runners.comment: Short-headed at Wetherby last month and this unexposed 7yo is a major player
runners.spotlight: Won in the autumn on first two chase starts (2m7f, good/good to soft; including here) then failed to stay 4m here in the Borders National; bounced back with short-head defeat at Wetherby (3m, soft) last month and there can be optimism he'll be fine at this shorter distance; major player.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very good work horse - an absolute aeroplane at home - but sometimes it does look too good to be true. We ran him in a bumper at Ludlow in April and hoped it would be a walk in the park but he got interfered with, got very lit up and hung quite badly, eventually running out. The ground proved to be too quick for him at Haydock on his next start and his wind caught him out at Chepstow in a good novice hurdle on his return this campaign. He's had a wind operation since and hopefully that'll sort him out. We think he's very smart and, if he gets his act together, he could be pretty formidable. 30-11-23

runners.comment: Won at Uttoxeter in January; disappointing since but this 5yo isn't written off
runners.spotlight: Won at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) in January when wearing first-time cheekpieces (retained) on his third chase start; disappointing since but this 5yo isn't written off today; won on good to soft ground on the Flat.

quotes.race: Champion Equestrian Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: My Noble Lord is a nice horse and he jumped really well. He'll be better suited by a more end-to-end gallop. He has a good attitude and should come forward from this - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, jockey.

quotes.race: Masons "Who Dares, Gins" Handicap
quotes.quote: My Noble Lord will just keep getting better and better. He's 540kg so he's a big unit that'll improve as he fills his frame hopefully.  We'll try him over further again. He was beaten over a longer distance at Wetherby, but he'll stay well. The ground is key, he wouldn't want summer fast ground. We don't have anything specific in mind, but there's that race at Haydock. Realistically he's not a July or August horse, though, so we could have a break - Michael Bell, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The Racecourse App Raceday Ready Handicap
quotes.quote: My Noble Lord has done well from two to three. He has a massive frame, he's taken a while to fill out and he's relished every inch of the mile and a half. I'd think he'll really start to flourish when we get him on some soft turf at a galloping track - Hector Crouch, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's going chasing and we'll try to benefit from his four-year-old allowance. He's jumping very well and looks really sharp. We've always thought a lot more of him than what he's shown. We're hoping he wasn't quite firing last season because he was a bit weak. 20-11-25

He ran as flat as a pancake last time at Newcastle in a better race and he'll come down in grade a bit now. He won the time before at Uttoxeter and has had a pretty good novice chase season overall. He's probably still got a bit in hand. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Course hurdle winner who was a good second over fences at Sandown recently; contender
runners.spotlight: Completed hurdle double when winning here (2m6f, soft) in December and tapped back into that promise when runner-up at Sandown (2m4f, soft) a fortnight ago on his third run over fences; won on good to soft going over hurdles; that latest form reads well and he's high on the list this afternoon.

quotes.race: Boyle Sports Now Open In Wetherby Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Glen Road is probably a three-miler, that's why we made plenty of use of him. He did it nicely. He'll probably have a go at chasing but I'm not entirely convinced he's a chaser - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He worked his way up and the handicapper probably got hold of him over hurdles, so he made a start over fences at Newcastle. He ran a bit keen and fell in a hole a bit, but jumped well, so we were happy with that. We'll find another chase for him soon. 28-01-26

runners.comment: Placed twice in a row in December and has had possible excuses on his last two starts
runners.spotlight: Placed twice in a row in December (2m4f/2m3f, soft/good to soft) and had an excuse (hampered) at Newcastle in January; heavy ground may have been against him here last time and he's not discounted now in cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: He won a Wexford bumper and was fourth over hurdles at Punchestown. He was bought to go chasing but should have a productive season as a hurdler. He's a big, strong horse who'll improve with time and hasn't shown his best yet. He has a very likeable attitude. 16-10-24

runners.comment: Won at Newcastle in January and heavy ground may not have suited here next time
runners.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in January on second chase start and heavy ground may not have suited here last month when a well-beaten third; this very lightly raced 7yo retains potential and could go well.

runners.comment: Twice made all in the autumn but progress has stalled on his last two outings
runners.spotlight: Twice made all in the autumn (2m3f, good) but his progress has stalled on his last two outings and he needs something extra if he's to return to winning ways today.

stable_tour.quote: A nice prospect who joined us after winning his bumper at Ballycrystal a year ago. He got off to a flyer when wining his bumper at Catterick in November and having come out of it well I hoped he would go well on his hurdling debut at Haydock the following month, but he was a little disappointing. The form of that race has worked out well, but my lad did a lot wrong - he was very keen and was in the air a long time when jumping his hurdles. He will have learned a lot there and is ready to go again. I hope he is not so babyish next time as he has ability and should be winning over hurdles sooner rather than later. 09-02-23

runners.breeder: Mrs Mossie Hayes & Mr Tom Hayes
runners.comment: Hit with 8lb rise for Musselburgh but had plenty in hand and could still be well treated
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Catterick in December on first two chase starts (2m3f, good to soft/good) and bounced back from lesser show at Haydock to win at Musselburgh (2m7f, soft) last month; hit with 8lb rise for last time but he had plenty in hand and could still be well treated.

quotes.race: Famous Five Handicap Chase (Go North Red Rum Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I got on Bridge Court as a spare ride about a month ago. It was over two and a half [miles] at Haydock and I was very confident afterwards that a step up in trip at an easier track would probably be right up his street. The form from Haydock worked out really well and he's a big horse who has probably taken a bit of time to come to hand. He loved the [soft] ground - Callum Bewley, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: A nice horse who's going to be a lovely novice chaser next season. He was very disappointing at Wetherby last time but before that ran a really nice race at Carlisle over a 2m1f trip that was too short for him. He's a lovely, big horse and maybe that Carlisle race took a bit more out of him than we thought, so he's having a bit of a break. 22-01-25

runners.owner: Miss Maria D Myco & John Johnson
runners.comment: Won first two chase starts; Newcastle defeat doesn't necessarily mean mark is beyond him
runners.spotlight: Won in January on first two chase starts (2m4f/2m3f, good to soft/soft), shaping each time as though he had more left in the tank; soundly beaten at Newcastle (2m, good to soft) since but that maybe shouldn't be taken as a sign that his current mark is beyond him; cheekpieces go on.

runners.owner: Mr & Mrs Jw Dale & & Mrs Jdj Copas
runners.comment: Well beaten last time when bidding for a four-timer; stamina to prove over new trip
runners.spotlight: Won three times in a row this winter (1m7f/2m, heavy-good to soft); made mistakes when well beaten at Newcastle (2m, good to soft) last time and his yard is in good form, but he needs to prove he can cope with his current mark, and also today's step up in trip.

quotes.race: pricedup.bet Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Stick With Me Sam is quite well bred and was second in this race last year, when his jumping went to pieces. He was brilliant at home, but once he got on the racecourse it all went a bit wrong. His jumping is still a work in progress, but you can see it's a lot better now - Tom Gretton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won a 2m5f chase round Cartmel but didn't really go when we took him back there. It turned out he'd picked up an injury, so he's on rest at the moment and will be out again in January. He wants good ground, so we'll see where we can find that. 29-10-25

racecards.verdict: Things clicked over fences for GLEN ROAD when he was runner-up at Sandown recently and he's taken to go one better today.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Diamond Dealer, 11/2 Glen Road, 13/2 Bridge Court, 7/1 My Noble Lord,  Moon Phases, 8/1 Always A Reason, 9/1 Defence Witness, 10/1 Joecooker, 12/1 Sleeping Satellite, 20/1 Stick With Me Sam

racecards.race_name: Remembering Duncan Davidson Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Goes well here but he's on a tough mark and has become very all or nothing
runners.spotlight: Won this last year and scored again here in November when in first-time blinkers (good to soft); however, he's on a tough mark and has become all or nothing; races prominently.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes 'Best Odds Guaranteed On Racing' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dropping back down in class helped him. He's a nice little horse. I feel sorry for Patrick on Your Own Story but Cadell probably had a little more toe on the day - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cadell is a horse we've always liked and we'd been looking forward to him stepping up to three miles over fences. He won two point-to-points and this was always going to be his game. You just dream that he'll eventually turn into a Scottish Grand National type, he likes good ground and stays very well. We're a long way off things like that but they have to be in the back of your mind, you can dream - Michael Scudamore, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's another nice staying chaser. We probably put him in at the deep end a couple of times the season before last, when he perhaps physically wasn't quite ready. His race was over at the second fence at Kelso on Saturday as his saddle slipped, but he'll still be aimed at the Borders National. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Mostly progressive chaser and feasible excuses when beaten 23l in the Eider
runners.spotlight: Did well last season; kicked off this campaign with a 3l win at Aintree (3m1f, good to soft) on Boxing Day and didn't run badly in valuable races on next two outings, last time in the Eider after which he was treated for post-race heat stress; he was joint-favourite for that and this race isn't as demanding.

quotes.race: William Hill Each Way Extra Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fortunate Man has done it well because he was lacking a run against the others. He had a good season last year and he's only a 6yo and could be the type for the regional Nationals - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Committed To Top Prices Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Fortunate Man can be a bit frustrating as he's good when he's good and awful when he's awful. He'll be a grand long-distance staying chaser - Jonjo O'Neill, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'd like to think he could improve a bit more with another year under his belt. I'm not sure where he'll start off yet, but he's better on soft ground and could be one for the regional nationals. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Back to form when second over 2m4f last time and now returns to a better trip
runners.spotlight: Last win was off a higher mark and he'll appreciate returning to further after chasing home a good thing over 2m4f at Ayr (soft; fine on good ground); that was a welcome return to form; definite chance if he can back it up.

quotes.race: Vesta Wealth Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dare To Shout thought he'd won the race after the last, but then they all came to him. To his credit, he stuck his neck out again. We always thought he'd stay three miles and, if anything, he's enjoyed the better ground today - Danny McMenamin, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Gordon Richards Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dare To Shout is not a big horse but I like the way he jumps as he's neat. He'll appreciate soft ground and three miles better - Ian Hamilton, owner.

quotes.race: Johnston Smillie Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: DARE TO SHOUT is a nice little horse. He did the job well and he'll jump a fence one day. Ian Hamilton speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: 2-5 over fences; still on a fair mark and open to further progress, he's a player
runners.spotlight: Has won two of his five chases and reportedly appreciated the drier surface (good to soft) when prevailing narrowly over 3m at Ludlow last time; off only 3lb higher and open to further progress, he's seriously considered.

stable_tour.quote: He won on his debut for us at Carlisle on Monday and there was a lot to like about the way he put his head down after the last. He's got some good point-to-point form and his work has been really good, so he looks smart. He could be one for a good handicap in the spring. 21-11-24

He probably needs better ground because when he had it last time at Ludlow and earlier on at Catterick, he jumped well and really picked up to win. Whereas on softer, he's struggled a bit. We may end up going for the Highland National at Perth. It's a step up in trip but he seems to stay really well. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Competitive mark but has to bounce back from a pretty poor run at Bangor
runners.spotlight: Strong stayer who was 6lb out of the weights when runner-up in the Scottish Borders National here in December; off the same mark for this but has to bounce back from a pretty poor run at Bangor; cheekpieces added.

quotes.race: BK Racing Hexham Marathon Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: There was a question mark over the trip but when Breeze Of Wind hit the front he pricked his ears - Sam Coltherd, jockey.

runners.comment: Recent Ayr winner; 4lb wrong so he's 9lb higher this time and in a stronger race to boot
runners.spotlight: Has made steady progress in the cheekpieces and would have won anyway last time at Ayr after being left clear late on (3m, soft); 4lb out of the weights so he's 9lb higher this time and in a stronger race to boot.

racecards.verdict: The O'Neills' FORTUNATE MAN returns to calmer waters after contesting the Eider and he wasn't seen to best effect that day.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Fortunate Man, 5/2 Blakey Boy, 3/1 Aboutdamntime, 6/1 Dare To Shout, 12/1 Breeze Of Wind, 14/1 Cadell

racecards.race_name: KOSB Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Solid record includes a C&D win; beat all bar the market leader at Newcastle last time
runners.spotlight: Solid record comprises two wins, including over C&D on penultimate start, and four second-place finishes; beat all bar the market leader at Newcastle (2m4f) most recently; major contender.

runners.comment: Drops back in class after Grade 2 attempt; won easily at Newcastle on penultimate start
runners.spotlight: Towards the rear when clipping heels and falling in Grade 2 at Kelso (2m2f) most recently; won easily at Newcastle (2m1f) the time before and enters calculations back down in class; dam stayed 3m1f.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well to come third in what was probably a nice novice hurdle at Ayr this month. He did best of the four-year-olds in the race - the other three either tailed off or pulled up - so we were pleased with him. He came to run a big race - he probably wouldn't have beaten the winner, as he just tired a little bit, which probably cost him second, but I think there was a lot to take out of it. He had previously fallen twice in point-to-points. He's a big horse who's still a little bit green and will need some racing, but I think he'll get there in the end. He's a bit of a playboy. 19-11-25

runners.breeder: Mrs Sandra Cozenot & Mr Herve Cozenot
runners.comment: Two from two, namely point/hurdle wins; promising southern raider who commands respect
runners.spotlight: Two from two, namely wins in Irish point and Chepstow maiden hurdle (2m3f) last year; promising southern raider who commands respect; declared 2:00 Newbury Friday.

quotes.race: BetWright Bet The Wright Way Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was very pleased with Le Frimeur. I'd have been disappointed if he'd got beaten, as he's a nice staying horse and didn't jump great early on, but just warmed to his task. He did it nicely with plenty in hand and I'm very pleased to get a winner for double green. I'm really grateful to be sent a horse from them and it's good to train them a winner. He'll keep improving and hopefully have a nice future - Harry Derham, trainer.

runners.comment: Has plenty to find
runners.spotlight: Consistent in bumpers, albeit with ordinary RPRs; couple of poorer results at Kelso since switched to hurdles; plenty to find.

runners.comment: Poor claims on form
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced 5yo who has poor claims on form; upped in trip.

runners.comment: Just an ordinary maiden and faces a stiffer task on these terms
runners.spotlight: Placed several times, including off a mark of 101 in Musselburgh handicap (2m4f) most recently; just an ordinary maiden and faces a stiffer task on these terms.

runners.comment: Beaten long way on the switch to rules
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in Irish point but beaten long way at Newcastle on the switch to rules; may be one for handicaps later on.

runners.comment: Below par at Ayr last time but runner-up over this C&D previously in his sole handicap
runners.spotlight: Better could have been expected in a maiden at Ayr last time but prior to that he was second of 12 over this C&D (good to soft) on his handicap debut, and he can be in the mix if returning to form.

runners.comment: Modest fourth at Kelso last time; needs improvement
runners.spotlight: Thrice-raced mare who may be suited by this new trip but has a lot to find on form; modest fourth at Kelso (2m) most recently.

racecards.verdict: Solid EAGLES REPRIEVE is first choice ahead of Gaelic Rover who drops back in class.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Eagles Reprieve,  Gaelic Rover, 4/1 The G Wizard, 13/2 Rememberthename, 16/1 Talk To The Boss, 25/1 Bollin Skittle, 66/1 Ivan's Legacy, 100/1 Melbourne Ghost

racecards.race_name: Racing Post+ Jodami Open NH Flat Race (Category 2 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Point/bumper winner; unplaced last time but fitting of hood may help this free-going sort
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt in points and followed up at Musselburgh on rules debut; only fifth (behind Diamond White) at Newcastle since but can't be written off; fitting of hood may suit this free-going sort.

runners.comment: Won his latest attempt in British points; sold for £60,000 since; check the betting
runners.spotlight: Raced twice in British points, winning three-finisher event at Sheriff Hutton latest; subsequently sold for £60,000; difficult to assess firmly but has potential; market may offer further guidance.

runners.comment: Gives the impression he may benefit from this switch to forecast faster ground
runners.spotlight: Failed to improve at Ayr kept to soft going but gives the impression he may benefit from this switch to forecast faster ground; half-brother to a bumper winner and progress remains possible.

runners.comment: Hung left but otherwise showed promise with third-place finish at Ayr; may progress
runners.spotlight: Spoiled his finishing effort by hanging left, possibly through greenness, but otherwise showed promise with his third of nine at Ayr; half-brother to a winner for his stable and looks open to progress.

runners.comment: Placed over C&D last time; this switch to faster ground may prompt further progress
runners.spotlight: Has taken a good hold in both starts but took a step forward with placed effort over C&D (heavy) latest and gives the impression this switch to forecast better ground may prove ideal; possibilities.
