runners.comment: Consistent thus far; third of 15 at Newcastle most recently; solid contender
runners.spotlight: Consistent thus far, having finished second in Irish point and third in two bumpers, latest in 15-runner field at Newcastle; very solid contender as things stand and may still have progress in her.

stable_tour.quote: Bought at the Cheltenham sale in March, she came from the same people who had Bill Joyce and they rated her highly. We'll probably start her off in a bumper in December and go from there. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Couple of fourth-place finishes at Ayr, beaten 49l latest; opposed
runners.spotlight: Couple of fourth-place finishes at Ayr, beaten 20l then 49l; the regress last time doesn't bode well and, on breeding, she's one for longer trips over jumps in due course.

runners.owner: Mrs J Porter And P Kirby
runners.comment: Sole 4yo in this field and interesting at the weights, with another step forward possible
runners.spotlight: Out of a dual winner in this sphere; raced twice in junior bumpers in the autumn, better effort when fourth at Aintree; sole 4yo in this field and interesting at the weights, with another step forward possible.

racecards.verdict: The suggestion is PRESENTANDCORRECT who ran well over C&D last time and may progress again. El Gangster is second pick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Diamond White, 7/2 Fridaysman, 5/1 King Kubala, 6/1 Presentandcorrect, 7/1 Kilaro, 8/1 Barito,  El Gangster, 25/1 Oor Wish

racecards.race_name: Castle Windows Newbury Anniversary Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: A Peltier, D Juste & J Houdin
runners.comment: Has built up a solid record at about 2m; ran well in the Dovecote most recently
runners.spotlight: Has built up a solid record when racing at about 2m under rules, as form figures of 222 this year help to demonstrate; ran well in the Dovecote at Kempton (good to soft) most recently; leading player back down in class.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in two strong bumpers last season, getting placed both times. He's come out and won his maiden hurdle at Fontwell this season, doing it very nicely. He has a tendency to jump to the right, but I feel very much he could be an EBF Final type. He'd go in the Sandown mud, which it generally what you get on that day, and I think he'd act on the track and would probably enjoy the trip. We'll try to get him qualified for that. 01-12-25

runners.comment: Brings strong form; beaten only a whisker dropped back to 2m last time; respected
runners.spotlight: Brings strong form, having made the frame in races won by the subsequent EBF Final and Supreme winners; beaten only a whisker at Exeter, the scene of his November win, dropped back to 2m last time; respected.

quotes.race: Radmore & Tucker, Stihl Garden Machinery Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I loved Lisbane Park at the Aintree Sale. I looked at them all and I said there is only one horse I want, and we managed to buy him and he wasn't that expensive in terms of what horses go for nowadays. He had been good at home and that was a lovely performance. He jumped great and travelled well and he put it to bed well. He pricked his ears going to the last, and popped it. He is a very likeable horse. I'd say we would take another small step with him as he has only run in one point-to-point and he is only a four-year-old as well. We are in no rush and I'm not going to put a target on his head - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Everything went smoothly at Exeter on Friday. He's only a four-year-old but he won his novice hurdle in great style. He's a really nice novice and he's definitely above average. There's an outside chance we could look at going to Ascot next week as he came out of his last race so well. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Latest Flat effort (stable debut) is notable form; brings potential to this code
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish unexposed sort whose Flat form comprises a success and two placed efforts, latest on debut for new stable in the AW novice event won by Constitution Hill; brings potential to this code and looks interesting.

stable_tour.quote: He's won on the Flat in Ireland and is a good type for two-mile novice hurdles in the spring. We'll give him plenty of time and if he were still a maiden this time next year it wouldn't be a problem. He's a progressive horse and could even go back on the Flat. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Twice-raced 6yo who may yet confirm the promise of his 2023 bumper win
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced 6yo who was possibly unsuited by soft going switched to hurdles three months ago; had wind surgery since; may yet confirm the promise of his good-ground bumper success in 2023.

stable_tour.quote: He won a junior bumper at Huntingdon for Tony Charlton - who's now my assistant - and he's joined us. He's had bit of an injury and he's only run the once, but he seems in good form at the moment. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Holds weak claims on form
runners.spotlight: Holds weak claims on bumper and hurdles form; should find handicaps more suitable shortly.

runners.comment: Rules form leaves a lot to be desired
runners.spotlight: Showed promise in the point-to-point sphere in 2023 but two rules efforts (in 2024 and 2026) leave a lot to be desired.

runners.comment: Pair of duck eggs next to his name
runners.spotlight: Pair of duck eggs next to his name; best watched.

runners.comment: Prevailed in juvenile hurdle over C&D last time; interesting at the weights
runners.spotlight: Flat scorer who has raced twice over hurdles, looking value for a bit more than the neck winning margin in juvenile event over C&D (good to soft) latest having idled in front; interesting contender at the weights.

racecards.verdict: Solid performers LISBANE PARK and Kocktail Bleu bring the best hurdles form, while Gambino and Cecilia Star add interest.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 Kocktail Bleu, 5/2 Lisbane Park, 3/1 Gambino, 11/2 Cecilia Star, 40/1 Giddyupadingdong, 100/1 King Berry,  Noble Don, 150/1 Padel Bandit

racecards.race_name: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 2nd of five in Doncaster handicap (extended 2m3f) two runs ago; needs to resume progress
runners.spotlight: Met with heavy defeats in a Grade 1 three starts back and a Grade 2 on latest but progressive form in his other three hurdle races, second of five in a handicap at Doncaster (extended 2m3f) on penultimate outing; needs to resume progress.

quotes.race: Eco-Power Group Novices' Hurdle (Go North Night Nurse Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Storming George is a seriously nice young horse who's always done everything right. I couldn't be more pleased to see him do it in that way. The form of his Newbury run was boosted on Friday and he's proved he goes on all ground as well. That was really impressive and he could be quite special. I'm not sure where we go next, but it's wonderful to find another gem for Peter. I'll chat to him about where we go. It might not be a Graded race next just yet, but he could work his way up the ladder - Neil King, trainer.

runners.comment: Tongue tied when running poorly last time and had wind surgery soon afterwards
runners.spotlight: Possibly best left-handed; either way, he ran poorly at right-handed Huntingdon last time, when some moderate jumps did not help; tongue tied that day (but not today) and had wind surgery soon afterwards; consistent form over hurdles before that run but needs better on this handicap debut.

quotes.race: RJS Waste Management UK Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fresh Perspective did an awful lot wrong and still won very impressively, so when he puts it all together I think he could be very good. He's a very talented horse with a huge engine and he's very exciting. We've only been schooling him on the all-weather, so he hasn't been out on the grass, and that showed today with his jumping being all at sea - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good horse who has a serious engine. He won a bumper on his debut, but then we ran him in a Listed race at Ascot and he completely boiled over in the preliminaries. He won on his hurdling debut at Fontwell last month and, if we can brush up his jumping, he could be smart. We might think about the Grade 2 at Haydock later this month. 05-11-25

runners.comment: Pulled up at Kelso latest but he was 28-1 in that Grade 2 and retains some interest
runners.spotlight: Won maiden at Musselburgh (2m4f, soft) in December and good second at Catterick (2m3f, good to soft) next time; pulled up at Kelso three weeks ago but he was 28-1 in that Grade 2 and retains some interest for this handicap debut.

quotes.race: Racing TV Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I suppose it was a match race on paper and I was happy to follow Derek [Fox, on Timefortom. I wanted to wait a bit longer to challenge him but we steadied up turning in and I'm surprised how well \BRed Oak\P quickened. Ascot was a decent race but, like every horse, they have to win and get confidence. It's a step back for a step forward. He did it really nicely and with his speed I wouldn't be against going back to two miles at some stage too - Jonathan Burke, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He was placed in bumpers in Ireland and is bred to do well. He looks like a nice new recruit to go hurdling with. 24-10-25

runners.comment: Longer trips will surely suit in due course but he's a useful prospect, at the least
runners.spotlight: Useful pedigree; second at Chepstow (good to soft) in December on debut and asserted late on in a novice at Taunton (heavy; at 4-5) in early February; both were over an extended 2m3f and longer trips than that will surely be his thing in due course, but he's a useful prospect (at the least) and probably on a favourable opening mark.

quotes.race: Racing To School Celebrates 25 Years Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Grand Vendetta was too backward to run in a bumper last season but he stays well and will eventually get three miles - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's an unraced half-brother to Sabrina, who won five races for us. He's been here some time and I've liked him from day one, despite niggling problems that have kept him off the track until now. Everyone who sits on him in the mornings likes him too and he should be ready to start off later this month. He'll have one run in a bumper, then go novice hurdling. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Comfortably on top in a 2m4f maiden at Hereford (soft; worst result was on good) last time
runners.spotlight: Ran at Hereford for bumper win and both hurdle races, comfortably on top in a 2m4f maiden (soft; worst result was on good) last time; this handicap debut demands plenty more but he's lightly raced and should retain potential.

runners.comment: Won two of four hurdle races, 2nd in the others; makes handicap debut on a reasonable mark
runners.spotlight: 0-3 in bumpers but he's won two of his four hurdle races and been runner-up in the others; second at Taunton (good) on penultimate start showed he stays 2m3f, before his narrow win at Exeter (2m, heavy) on latest; makes handicap debut on a reasonable mark.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse. I was actually pleased with his bumper campaign, even though he didn't win one. We pitched him into a £10,000 race at Haydock on his final bumper start and we went there thinking he'd run well, which he did (fifth behind So Proud), but the race wasn't run to suit. I was never disappointed, although you would say his hurdle form is far better. He won on his first run over hurdles at Newton Abbot, then split two nice horses of JP McManus's (Harry Lowes and Aguellid) down at Exeter. Then, last time out, he bumped into another in-form horse of Paul Nicholls' called Calvino at Taunton. Where's he going to go now? Well, I think we'll go for another novice under a penalty - the handicapper has quite rightly given him a mark of 118 - as I don't think he's quite ready for the hustle and bustle of handicaps yet. If everything was right he might go for one of those nice novice handicaps at Sandown in the spring because he's a horse who would handle a bit of good ground. He's a nice type who will jump a fence in time as well. 21-01-26

runners.comment: Seemingly stretched when he tried 2m4f; hurdling score is 1-7 and he may prove vulnerable
runners.spotlight: Has seen much more action than most of this field and took a novice at Chepstow (2m, soft) in November; second in handicap here (2m, good to soft) was the clear best of his last three outings (seemingly stretched by 2m4f the time before) and this looks a competitive mark, but his hurdling score is 1-7 and he may well prove vulnerable to an improver.

stable_tour.quote: He was third in a good race at Chepstow before he unseated at Fontwell last time. It was unfortunate but it happened too far from home to know if he was going to run well at the time. He could still be a nice horse this season and we'll keep him at two miles for now. He goes to Chepstow on Friday. 20-11-25

runners.comment: Early days but markedly better is needed; poor show on handicap debut (near 2m2f, heavy)
runners.spotlight: Won a maiden at Plumpton (2m5f, good to soft) in December on hurdling debut; put firmly in his place next time, while appearing to run creditably, and needs to bounce back from a poor show on handicap debut at Fontwell (near 2m2f, heavy) four weeks ago; early days but markedly better is needed.

stable_tour.quote: Won his bumper well at Fontwell in May and is set to go novice hurdling. He should be a nice horse for the winter and I expect him to win races. There's no rush to step him up in trip, but as he progresses we can creep up in distance. 28-10-25

runners.comment: Drew 12l clear for breakthrough win at Doncaster (extended 2m3f, good to soft); up 8lb
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in nine of his first 14 races, before finally off the mark when well backed for 12-runner handicap at Doncaster (extended 2m3f, good to soft) three weeks ago in second-time cheekpieces; drew 12l clear for that breakthrough but this 8lb higher mark seems to demand another step forward.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I wouldn't call Diamond Koda ungenuine. He's been a bit unlucky, his jumping has let him down mainly, he's fluffed a hurdle at crucial parts of races. He wasn't right last time, he scoped dirty after that and we thought we'd got him right for today. We were pretty hopeful - Nick Kent, trainer.

runners.comment: Progressive juvenile hurdler; this longer trip could suit him very well on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: 2m win on his second French Flat start; progressive form in his three forays over hurdles for new connections, notably when winning at Chepstow (2m, soft) and runner-up at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) in another juvenile event; this longer trip could suit him very well on handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: He came from France having won over two miles on the Flat and he's very well. He's a good jumper and we're well schooled now. He'll be in the front row among our juvenile hurdlers. 21-10-25

racecards.verdict: The slightly shorter trip on drying ground may make GRAND VENDETTA's task a bit more tricky but he may also be the best prospect.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Fresh Perspective, 9/2 Thewoodcorner, 5/1 Grand Vendetta, 11/2 Storming George, 7/1 Glancing Jack, 8/1 Doctors Hill, 12/1 Red Oak, 14/1 Kapitein Kool,  Diamond Koda, 16/1 The Boss Bear

racecards.race_name: BetVictor Home Of The Saturday Superboost Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Hindered by being unable to dominate last time; chance hinges on getting an easy lead
runners.spotlight: Two wins from the front, including a defeat of Heltenham over C&D, and two non-completions comprise a mixed current campaign; hindered by being unable to dominate in the Greatwood Gold Cup last time; chance may depend on whether he gets an easy lead.

stable_tour.quote: He was unfortunate on New Year's Day ? he's a good jumper but just made a mistake. He prefers quicker ground and may run in the Greatwood Gold Cup at Newbury in a couple of weeks, so he's only a possible for the festival. He'd have to go and win very well there to justify his entry in the Ryanair. 15-02-26

He won his point-to-point last December in the style of a nice horse and I was confident before his Hereford bumper last spring. He won nicely by 12 lengths and followed up under a penalty at Haydock on his only other start. That was a good performance and augurs well for this term. He has schooled beautifully, and I am looking at starting him back at Fakenham on Friday, ground permitting. I rate him as an exciting prospect and the plan is to start small before stepping up in grade. 13-10-22

runners.comment: Has a doubt over current form; second start for new stable
runners.spotlight: Useful on his day for Willie Mullins but form has dipped this winter, most recently last of four finishers at Doncaster where he was the rank outsider on debut for new yard; best watched unless the market signals go the other way.

quotes.race: BetVictor Proud Sponsors Of Irish Racing Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: It was a very good performance. Lucid Dreams kept him honest the whole way and Mark had to go to plan B and drop him in behind. Hercule De Seuil jumped well when Mark needed him to over the last four fences. I haven't decided if we'll go further with him but if the weather stays dry, we might get another run into him. We might give him a mid-season break then and come back in the spring. I'd rather keep to the minimum trip but he could go out to two and a half. Mark felt he maybe doesn't want the ground as soft as it was today - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Ballymore Group Irish EBF Kilbegnet Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Hercule Du Seuil is surprising us all the time and seems to be improving with every run. He's very sharp and likes getting on with it. He seems to really like his new job. I have a feeling there is more improvement to come from him as well. I'm not sure he's a real winter horse but we'll keep going as long as we can with him and try to find something suitable for him now. Hopefully he can continue to surprise us - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Mark [Walsh] thinks Hercule Du Seuil is settling and learning to relax. That will help him see out longer trips and have more at the end of his races - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Join The Tipperary Supporter's Club (C & G) Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was a weak race. Hercule du Seuil is a forward-going horse and so we made the running and nothing really came to me. There is an engine there - he was very free last year, but is starting to settle now and is growing up with every run - Mark Walsh, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He is a winner at Navan and seems to like the place so it makes sense to run in the rescheduled Fortria Chase on Monday. We'll see how he goes in that before planning where to go next. 17-11-25

runners.owner: Chris & Giles Barber And P J Vogt

prev_owners.owner: P K Barber And P J Vogt

runners.comment: Very attractively treated on historical data, which includes Grade 2 wins; one to consider
runners.spotlight: Heavy ground provides an excuse for latest effort; has hinted at retaining ability otherwise since returning from lengthy layoff; very attractively treated on historical data, which includes four Grade 2 wins (bumper/hurdles/fences); one to consider.

quotes.race: Boodles "Rising Stars" Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was brilliant. Knappers Hill could possibly go to Newbury next (for the John Francome Novices' Chase) - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Select Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were a bit worried about the ground and we were in one mind whether to run him or not, because the only time Knappers Hill has been disappointing was here in the EBF Final on soft ground. We rode him different today and just took our time, I said to Bryony to let him creep into things and hope they don't go too quick and see if he gets the trip and he did. He'll go chasing next year, he'll be a nice type for things like the Rising Stars at Wincanton so we're looking forward to that now - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Unibet Elite Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was fairly obvious the only way we were going to win was by going a gallop. Knappers Hill jumped well, which was brilliant. He stays well. He is a good horse and he is improving. He obviously stays and we took the race to them. I was just worried a fraction about his jumping, but he is brilliant now. He is obviously a smart horse - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Wasdell Group Silver Trophy Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Knappers Hill is quite sharp. It's good to see him gallop all the way to the line over two and a half [miles] and the horse is not short of speed so where we go next, I don't know. He's going to go up now and I always half had in my mind to go to Wincanton [Elite Hurdle] with him. I just think a fast-run race and of the horses I've won with before he'd favour with those. The faster they go the better he'd be. I don't know what we do but he's quite progressive and looks an interesting hurdler. He won't go chasing just yet - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Novices' Championship Final Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Knappers Hill is a really nice horse. We knew we had to qualify at Newton Abbot last week so I kept him fresh for that and that race brought him on a bit today. He has done that nicely off top weight. He was sixth in the Betfair Hurdle of 135 and a bit of inexperience that got him behind and on that form he was going to be hard to beat today. He loves good ground and running him in the EBF Final was an error but the owners were keen to go as they didn't want to go to Cheltenham with him. It didn't do him any harm and we just waited for better ground. Something like the Gerry Feilden would be a good starting point next season - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: EBF Stallions "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a racecourse school for Knappers Hill really but we've got a bit more experience. He needed it as he's been a bit fresh but he's learning all the time. We'll now go in a better race somewhere where he can get a lead. The Kennel Gate [at Ascot] would suit him and is an option. I always thought we'd have a couple of runs then go there but we'll see. I'm not convinced he'd want the ground too deep as he's a speedy horse. That would be a perfect race for him - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Andy Stewart Racing's Great Friend Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Knappers Hill will go to Wincanton on November 6 for another novice hurdle. He needs experience and was a bit keen and green there. He's a bit of a baby and two miles is fine for now. He's got enough boot, but just needs to sharpen up his jumping. He'll be better in a bigger field, getting a good gallop and he can follow them. He'll keep improving, but I honestly wouldn't know how far because he surprised me last year. He'll go on any ground - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Enter ITV7 Tonight Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Harry Cobden chose to ride Stage Star because he'd won on the soft at Chepstow, but if he'd have run on quicker ground at Chepstow - like Knappers Hill did - he'd have won as well. There isn't much between them and the idea with Knappers Hill would be to go to Aintree for the Grade 2 bumper at the Grand National meeting and not do anything in between. I think they want three bumper runs and then go hurdling. He's schooled already and does everything nicely - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Wasdell Group Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Knappers Hill is one of loads of 4yos we've to run. He'll stay in bumpers this season and go hurdling this time next year - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It's great to have him back after the best part of two years off the track. He's been in since the start of July and we had hoped to run him back over hurdles in the Silver Trophy at Chepstow last month but conditions had quickened up. Although he does act on any ground, you wouldn't want to take any risks after the problems he's had. He'll be back chasing now, although after two runs he won't be the easiest to place. His handicap mark is definitely on the high side for what he has achieved over fences. Graduation chases are a real help to a horse like him who lacks experience, and there's one at Haydock on Betfair Chase day I've got my eye on. Understandably, after such a long time off he was pretty rusty to begin with, but he's starting to come together nicely now and we took him to Newbury for a racecourse gallop a week ago. 04-11-25

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late N W Lake

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late N W Lake

runners.comment: Suited by this C&D; back to form in the Greatwood Gold Cup; won this race in 2023 and 2024
runners.spotlight: Back to something like his best last time, registering a second success in the Greatwood Gold Cup and taking C&D record to 4-6; won this contest in 2023 and 2024; back up the weights but commands respect kept to a scenario that suits him ideally.

quotes.race: BetVictor Greatwood Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham has fallen a couple of times, but he's only a couple of pounds higher than when he won this race two years ago. We knew that if his jumping came together, there was no reason why he couldn't be competitive. He's clearly got an affiliation with this place. He's got his jumping issues, but in a fast-run race on soft ground, he just gets into a better rhythm, and it's great he's been able to do that - Nick Pearce, trainer's representative.It's extraordinary when you look at the races Heltenham has been in this season, especially last time at Ascot. It's a good training performance, and he obviously likes it around here. He travelled so well, but we wanted to take our time and get into a rhythm, and get him jumping. I thought he'd definitely stay, and he had as good a chance as everyone - Charlie Todd, jockey.

quotes.race: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham won over hurdles at the start of the season and maybe had a hard race, but he definitely had a hard race at Aintree after that on bad ground. Before Kempton in February, his coat massively changed and I knew he hadn't been right. He's come into form and is pretty effective round here and we'll look at all sorts of races. Maybe Sandown and the Oaksey Chase will suit him at the end of the season, a big galloping track. If a Bravemansgame turns up in that, he isn't in his league, but there's a race at Perth for him and options at Ayr and he's in the Topham too - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Dransfields CIU Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham was back over hurdles and it was a bit different for him. His jumping has never been his forte, back over hurdles he was knocking them but he's gone and done the job and that's the main thing - Tristan Durrell, jockey.

quotes.race: Run For Your Money At BetVictor Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham is improving all the time and hopefully keeps improving. Chasing has helped him but time more than anything. I could see him one day coming here for a Coral Gold Cup, but that might be in 2024 rather than the autumn. More immediately, he could go to Sandown on the last day of the season for a novice handicap chase, but it would have to keep raining. He wants really slow ground, it's very important to him - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's done us proud over the years and hopefully there's another half-decent day in him. It all came together for him at the end of last season and he ran very well at Fontwell last time, although he's probably a little too high in the handicap at the moment. A big, strong-travelling horse, he wants to go left-handed on a galloping track on softer ground. He may go to Wetherby on November 15 and I hope there's another decent race in him. 10-11-25

runners.owner: G R Orchard & Mrs J M Gray
runners.comment: Has looked as good as ever in winning two of his last three races; likely player
runners.spotlight: Northern runner who has looked as good as ever in winning two of his last three races, taking chase record to 6-18; did it quite readily at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) latest; ran respectably at Newbury in November; likely player in current form.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You could blame the track last time at Cheltenham but the whole yard had a dip in form around then and I think that was it. Prairie Wolf was good again there and could go to Ayr - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Prairie Wolf last time in a deeper race at Newbury and he ran really well, and I got an easy ride off him today. He jumped really well, which was key, and enjoyed the ground - Jack Tudor, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Extra Places Every Day Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Prairie Wolf has gone over a shorter trip because of the ground. He was running a strong race at Carlisle , it was just one of those racing errors. I'd like to think he can go and win a couple more this season and the two-and-a-half mile handicap at the Cheltenham Festival would be the aim - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He has improved again this season and was a good winner at Aintree on Boxing Day. He went down to Cheltenham last Saturday and it was a very competitive race. We were happy with him going there and we'll take stock and make another plan. Earlier in his career he got lost over hurdles, but it changed when he saw a fence and he won three chases in his novice season. He had his wind done at the start of the season, which has improved him again. Two and a half miles on good to soft ground is perfect for him. 28-01-26

prev_owners.owner: K Leggett, Susan And John Waterworth

runners.comment: Good second in this race last year, prior to beating Heltenham at Newton Abbot
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent this season but has finished a good second on two occasions (November/December) and filled the same position in this race 12 months ago prior to beating Heltenham at Newton Abbot; well capable of posing a threat, provided he's back to form.

quotes.race: Bob Champion Cancer Trust Sussex Champion Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Scarface took two or three runs to really get the hang of jumping, but the last two runs he's travelled and jumped well. Today was smooth all the way, he looked the winner some way out. I always thought he'd improve for fences. He'll have to go up in grade after that. He's still a novice this year, so we'll probably take him to Sandown at the end of the season and then step him up in trip next year - Joe Trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Serial Winners Fund Novices' Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've gone a nice gallop and Scarface's travelled and jumped brilliantly. He's had a tendency to down tools at certain parts of the race in the past but today he was on fire. Joe said today was his Gold Cup and he was right - Brendan Powell, jockey.

quotes.race: raceshare.com Racehorse Shares From £39 Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We bought Scarface as a store so he's taken time. Tactically we went for races last season that if he won, they were nice pots, but recognised he might not and then we'd have a full season as a novice. There was no mad rush and he's a chaser, a three-mile one I think. Joe will be in charge of race planning, but we could go for better novice races. He was rated 128 and we think he's a bit better than that - he'll be better in a better race, he wants to be covered up and towed along as he's got a high-cruising speed. What doesn't suit him is small fields and leading - all what he's just done! - Richard O'Dwyer, part-owner.

stable_tour.quote: He got the trip well in the Badger Beers last weekend on his first try over three miles. The handicapper hasn't touched him, so the Peter O'Sullevan could be an option at Newbury. 12-11-25

I was thrilled he won at Plumpton last time, although they'd dropped him to a nice mark. He took a few runs to get the hang of things over fences, but - in fairness to him - got murdered everywhere he went in the race before that win. He won like he's capable of, jumping like a stag in cheekpieces. I'm hopeful he can go forward from that and there should be more to come. 18-01-24

runners.comment: Absent for 22 months; faller in two of his four chase attempts; comes with risk
runners.spotlight: On an attractive mark but comes with risk, having fallen in two of his four attempts over fences and been absent since performing below market expectations at Warwick 22 months ago; the betting may offer further guidance.

quotes.race: Brian Giles Memorial "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Authorised Speed to finish fifth in the Champion Bumper and I said then I thought he was a proper horse. He finds everything so easy and doesn't get stressed. He's a proper soft-ground horse and hopefully he can come back here for the Tolworth - that would be the target at the moment - Josh Moore, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Don't Miss A Beat With Free RacingTV Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We've taken our time with Authorised Speed and the hopes were high, but then you see Mr Nicholls here and he's just got one runner. I'll leave plans to Gary, who'll place him, but the thing was to win a bumper - Pat Gallagher, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He jumped foot-perfect until the second-last and was going to win when he took a silly fall on his chase debut at Ascot last season. Plumpton was probably the wrong place to run him after that and things happened too quickly for him around there. He'll run predominantly over two and a half miles and upwards this season on stiff tracks. I think he could progress over fences and he schooled very well last week. I remember finishing fifth on him in the Champion Bumper a few years ago and was cantering going down the hill, but he's only just filling into himself and he's certainly got an engine. Long term, something like the Turners at the festival might be his type of race now it's a handicap. He could start back at Ascot on Saturday but only if the ground is soft enough. 29-10-24

I really do like this horse who is still a big baby. He started the season with a good second in a Listed Ascot bumper and put that experience to good use when winning with his head in his chest at Newbury last month. I am not sure what he beat but Paul Nicholls and Alan King trained the placed runners. We have some big ambitions here as there is a Listed bumper at Newbury coming up which he goes for next, and if he comes through that well then I would certainly consider the Cheltenham Bumper. 02-02-22

runners.comment: Saved for spring ground; scored under Sean Bowen on penultimate appearance
runners.spotlight: Absent since suffering a heavy defeat over 3m in November; seemingly saved for spring ground and could go well with Sean Bowen back on board; sole attempt under this rider resulted in Market Rasen success (2m5f) on penultimate start.

quotes.race: LK Bennett Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Coastguard Station is quite a quirky individual, hence why he has the headgear on. Even though he's keen, he can often get there and think he's done enough - Henry Oliver, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We'd given Coastguard Station a little break as he's quite a free individual and can flatten himself out. He's come back fresh and well and that was ideal. We'll see what's about and see how he is. He likes a fast run race and could go up in trip with a run behind him - Henry Oliver, trainer.

quotes.race: More Than A Flake Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Henry (Brooke) gave Coastguard Station a proper educational ride. He has loads of experience and he's very underrated as he was more than capable of getting the job done and we were pleased to have him on board. I don't think he wants the ground too extreme, so we might look for something this side of Christmas before then looking at nicer racing in the spring - Henry Oliver, trainer.

racecards.verdict: C&D specialist HELTENHAM (nap) is taken to land this prize for the third time. Scarface is second pick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Heltenham, 9/2 Knappers Hill, 5/1 Prairie Wolf, 13/2 Twinjets, 8/1 Hercule Du Seuil,  Scarface, 10/1 Coastguard Station, 12/1 Authorised Speed

racecards.race_name: BetVictor British EBF "National Hunt" Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Limited Handicap) (Grade 2) (GBB)

runners.comment: Has top weight on this handicap debut but this new trip could prove just the ticket
runners.spotlight: 3-5 in bumpers, including a Sandown Listed win on good to soft; won at Chepstow (2m, soft) on third attempt over hurdles and runner-up in the other three; cheekpieces latest (ran creditably); has top weight on this handicap debut but going beyond 2m1f for first time could prove just the ticket.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Mares' Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Charisma Cat didn't seem to handle the bends very well, but she has come back on the bridle. She wouldn't want this ground as it is hard work on the hurdle track. We all felt the one at Market Rasen was one that got away, but she didn't handle the track at all. She got shuffled well back, but she would have won in another couple of strides. We made up for it today, and we got a win, and some black type. If we are happy she will go to Aintree - Alan King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a homebred of the Waley-Cohen family, by Nathaniel, who's one of the most exciting stallions out there, and she won well at Southwell in the summer. She had a break but has come back into strong work and will have another run in a bumper, but we definitely think she's above average. 25-10-24

She's a homebred of the Waley-Cohen family, by Nathaniel who's one of the most exciting stallions out there, and won well at Southwell in the summer. She had a break but has come back into strong work and will have another run in a bumper but we definitely think she's above average. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Fluffed the final flight last time; open to further progress on this handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Tongue tied and made most when clearcut winner at Ludlow (2m5f) and excellent second of 16 at Warwick (2m3f, again good to soft); fluffing the final flight relinquished the initiative last time (Edith Pelham third, Shotgun Shirley fourth) and she's open to further progress on this handicap debut.

runners.comment: Ran well behind Charisma Cat latest; has more to offer, including at this longer trip
runners.spotlight: Won at Huntingdon on penultimate start; soundly beaten behind Charisma Cat in a Listed race here the time before but put up a far better show against that rival when they were placed at Market Rasen on latest outing; they are closely matched judged on latest result and she has more to offer, including at this longer trip.

quotes.race: pricedup.bet Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Mares' Novices' Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Watamu was a bit keen at Newbury last time but settled better today and the Grade 2 EBF Mares' Handicap Final back there in March might be a suitable target - Emma Lavelle, trainer.

runners.comment: Never got to grips with two of today's rivals latest (2m) but one to note given her yard
runners.spotlight: Marked improvement to win at Windsor in January in her third hurdle race; came from off the pace when fourth of nine at Market Rasen (again 2m, soft) and never got to grips with today's rivals Charisma Cat and Watamu, a result which leaves her with something to find but this is a different trip and her trainer is a dab hand at big handicap wins.

stable_tour.quote: She won a bumper last year but was a little keen on her hurdling debut at Worcester last month. She'll be seen to much better effect off a faster pace, and she has plenty of speed for two miles. 10-11-25

runners.breeder: Earl De Cordelles & Earl La Dariole
runners.comment: Already a 2m5f winner before she won at Wincanton (1m7f) 16 days ago; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Won at Warwick (2m5f, good to soft; from Fresh As A Daisy) on second start under rules; floundered in Grade 2 on heavy there next time but no ill effects, as she asserted on run-in at Wincanton (1m7f, good to soft) 16 days ago; back up in trip for this handicap debut and remains capable of better.

runners.comment: Going the right way over hurdles (2m4f/2m5f); this is a strong race for handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Did well in bumpers and going the right way over hurdles, on last two starts winning at Southwell (2m4f, good to soft) and second at Wincanton (2m5f, heavy); needs further progress in this good race for handicap debut.

quotes.race: Fancave Cheltenham Preview Here 6th March Mares' Open NH Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Strong Run is lovely and her owners have been so patient with her, which has been key. She ran exceptionally well at Cheltenham and she deserved this. I'm delighted with Highland Haven as well. She put a bad run behind her the last day. They're both lovely mares and can both go to Aintree. It's good timing after today and both of them could be better in the spring - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

runners.comment: Won at Southwell (2m5f, soft) latest, battling back after a bad mistake at final flight
runners.spotlight: Trailed several of today's rivals at Market Rasen in her second hurdle race but showed that to be all wrong when winning at Southwell (2m5f, soft) 19 days ago, battling back after a bad mistake at the final flight; better is needed for this handicap debut and cheekpieces are added.

quotes.race: Racing TV Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a great start and Edith Pelham will improve for the run. She's been a dream to train. She probably wants proper soft ground and the obvious thing is to roll on to Cheltenham for the mares' Listed race [in November] - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

runners.breeder: N J Henderson And Mrs S A Aston
runners.comment: Chased home Indannya at Warwick (2m5f) last time; more to offer on this handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Made a winning hurdle debut at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last May and put reappearance behind her when chasing home Indannya at Warwick (2m5f, good to soft) on New Year's Eve; more to offer on this handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: Life has been tough for her. She was always getting little niggly problems and was a bit fragile, but we've worked through it. She was too old for bumpers earlier this year, so we sent her over hurdles at Uttoxeter in May and she won nicely. She'll be a novice this season and she can go well. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Work to do but strong impression of long-term potential, including over this longer trip
runners.spotlight: Three runs over hurdles, all in the mud and her best result when second to Charisma Cat at Chepstow (2m, soft) in January; made most when well beaten behind her and several more of today's rivals at Market Rasen on latest start; major work to do but she leaves one of the strongest impressions of long-term potential, including over this longer trip.

stable_tour.quote: It was disappointing when we ran her at Hexham two runs ago [beaten at odds-on]. I wasn't at all surprised at being second behind Charisma Cat at Chepstow last time, but I was more surprised at being beat at Hexham after she'd run well first time out at Carlisle. She's declared to run at Market Rasen on Tuesday. Hopefully she'll go well. 18-02-26

runners.breeder: G Durrheim And Maria Mulcahy Durrheim
runners.comment: 1-9 hurdling; 5lb lower than when 4th under M Dodd at Cheltenham December, her best form
runners.spotlight: Held up; 1-9 over hurdles but 5lb lower than when fourth under Murray Dodd at Cheltenham (2m4f, good to soft) in December, her best form; no match for Indannya or Fresh As A Daisy at Warwick next time, but her latest start (pulled up at Ludlow; tongue tied first time) is the chief worry.

runners.comment: Much further behind Edith Pelham at Southwell last time; early days for handicap debutante
runners.spotlight: Progressed well in bumpers and ran encouragingly behind Betty's Daisy and Edith Pelham when fourth of 16 at Warwick (2m3f, good to soft) on second start over hurdles; she was much further behind Edith Pelham at Southwell 19 days ago, but these are early days for this handicap debutante.

stable_tour.quote: She won a bumper at Uttoxeter in October and has been second in two more, including last time in a Listed bumper at Cheltenham on Paddy Power day. She was meant to be going to Fontwell on Monday for a mares' novice hurdle, but she missed that and will probably go to Huntingdon just before Christmas. She's been schooling very well and I'm really excited by her. She comes from a wonderful family, being a half-sister to five winners including Martello Sky. She's my dark horse. 10-12-25

runners.owner: Hot To Trot Jumping And Dahlbury
runners.comment: Not the most persuasive evidence but this handicap debut should give her a better chance
runners.spotlight: About 11l fourth to Betty's Daisy at Ludlow (2m5f, good to soft) on second start over hurdles; a bit better when coming from the rear for sixth of 12 at Market Rasen (near 2m5f, soft) on latest, which isn't the most persuasive evidence but this handicap debut should give her a better chance.

runners.comment: Backward steps on last two starts leave her with plenty to prove; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Ex-French 5yo who won British debut at Windsor (2m, good to soft) in November; backward steps at Uttoxeter (2m6f, heavy) and Carlisle (extended 2m3f, good to soft) leave her with more to prove than plenty of these, although it is her handicap debut.

runners.comment: Dual bumper winner; second on latest start was at least her best show in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Won two bumpers last term on good to soft; she's failed to match that form over hurdles but second of six on handicap debut at Wetherby (extended 2m3f, soft) last time was at least her best show in this sphere.

stable_tour.quote: She's as tough as old boots and ended the season by winning the £20,000 bumper on Midlands National day at Uttoxeter. She goes out and runs her race every time. There's no fuss about her and she just gets on with the job. She'll probably end up being a two-and-a-half-miler over hurdles and hopefully will do very well. 22-10-25

runners.comment: Won at Carlisle (extended 2m3f); has big swing in the weights with Indannya from Wincanton
runners.spotlight: Won at Carlisle (extended 2m3f, good to soft) in February on second start over hurdles; 13l third to Indannya at Wincanton (1m7f) was better on RPRs and there's a big swing in the weights for today's handicap debut.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Mares' "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (EBF Mares' NH Nov' Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Sevarana is only small but she's a tough girl. She's taken a bit of time to come to hand - like her brother Sevarano who was talented but we lost in the Reynoldstown during Covid - but she is improving and learning to settle now. The EBF Mares' Final at Newbury is a nice race to aim at and will certainly be fun. All credit must go to Richard [Bandey, trainer], who felt the ground wasn't right for her at Kempton yesterday so drove the box up to Carlisle himself and put in the hard yards - Tim Syder, joint-owner.

runners.comment: Lacks any solid claims for this handicap debut; tongue tied first time
runners.spotlight: Has shown a bit of ability in her three points and the two completions over hurdles, but those 18l and 19l defeats in this sphere don't present any solid claims for today's handicap debut; tongue tied first time.

racecards.verdict: It's a fascinating puzzle but the vote goes to INDANNYA ahead of Charisma Cat, Trinity Street and Fresh As A Daisy.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Getawhisky, 5/1 Strong Run, 13/2 Charisma Cat,  Fresh As A Daisy, 8/1 Indannya, 9/1 Watamu, 12/1 Betty's Daisy, 14/1 Queenofthejukebox, 16/1 Trinity Street,  Pismo Beach, 20/1 Shotgun Shirley, 22/1 Edith Pelham, 33/1 Gaelic Saint,  Future Bucks, 50/1 Ballynorth

racecards.race_name: Goffs Hundred Grand Bumper (An Open National Hunt Flat Race) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 2-2 last summer but concedes weight all round and has plenty to find on the figures
runners.spotlight: Unbeaten at Bangor (good) and Stratford (good to firm) last summer; may still be unexposed but he concedes weight all round and has plenty to find on the figures after seven months off.

runners.comment: Ready 10l winner on debut at Doncaster; open to improvement and high on the list
runners.spotlight: Out of a mare who won a bumper, and he made a really encouraging debut when readily accounting for six rivals at Doncaster (soft; 5-2 favourite; by 10l) in January; open to improvement and high on the list for a trainer-jockey combination that won this race 12 months ago.

runners.comment: 15l winner at Chepstow on second start, making all; should put up another bold show
runners.spotlight: Built significantly on debut form when winning at Chepstow (soft; 13-2) in January by 15l, always in front and surging clear from over 1f out; today's conditions are likely to be less testing but he should still put up another bold show.

stable_tour.quote: Last month he won a Chepstow bumper by 15 lengths, no less. I was really pleased because it was a step up from his debut, also at Chepstow, when he came fourth. He was bought at Goffs as a three-year-old store and has been worth the wait. He's now eligible for Newbury's Goffs Hundred Grand Bumper on March 21. Soft ground is a must for this big sort. 25-02-26

runners.breeder: E A R L Guittet Desbois
runners.comment: Just shaken up to win at Kempton; major player for trainer with fine record in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Showed promise on debut over C&D and duly progressed to beat 13 opponents at Kempton (good to soft) last month, travelling well and just shaken up to assert; major player for a trainer with a fine record in this sphere.

runners.comment: Blotted copybook with wayward display over C&D last time and needs to get back on track
runners.spotlight: Debut winner at Wincanton (good) but blotted his copybook with a wayward display in C&D Listed event (heavy; 17-2) six weeks ago and needs to get back on track.

runners.comment: Pulled up in point; interesting that connections throw him in at deep end for rules debut
runners.spotlight: £26,000 3yo; by Order Of St George; dam bumper winner; pulled up on his only go in points but interesting that connections throw him in at the deep end for rules debut; worth monitoring in the market.

runners.breeder: A McGladdery, Ka Bloodstock & S Kemble
runners.comment: Fits the bill on pedigree but made no impact on debut at Kempton; improvement required
runners.spotlight: Fits the bill on pedigree (by Walk In The Park out of a bumper/2m hurdle winner) but he made no impact on debut at Kempton (good to soft; 22-1) four weeks ago; needs to have learned a lot in a short space of time.

runners.comment: Good fifth in Cheltenham Listed event; doesn't have much to find and may progress further
runners.spotlight: Much better effort so far when fifth in Listed event at Cheltenham (soft) in November, fading after racing freely; looks the stable's second string on jockey bookings but he doesn't have much to find on form and may progress further.

stable_tour.quote: I thought he might win his first bumper but he ran well in second and he's getting stronger. We'll probably stick to bumpers this year and he's eligible for a £100,000 race in the spring, which may be where we'll aim him. I think he's smart. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Followed last-gasp Wincanton win with fine third at Cheltenham; has to be considered
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to the high-class jumper Romeo Coolio; got up late on to make winning debut at Wincanton in November and improved markedly when third in Listed race at Cheltenham (good ground) on New Year's Day; yard does well in bumpers and won this race in 2023; has to be considered.

runners.comment: Debut winner at Carlisle; more needed to hold his own against much stronger opposition
runners.spotlight: Dug deep to make winning start at Carlisle (good to soft; 4-1) in February; however, that form doesn't look anything special and he'll need to progress to hold his own against today's much stronger opposition.

runners.comment: Good late work when fourth at Warwick; progress needed but that's not out of the question
runners.spotlight: Nicely bred daughter of Telescope; did her best work late on when 10l fourth of 13 at Warwick (good to soft; 11-2) four months ago; improvement required to trouble some of these but that's not out of the question.

runners.owner: DL Adams, JA Adams & G McPherson
runners.comment: Met trouble in bunch finish at Ascot; no surprise if she improves fair bit with more luck
runners.spotlight: Only seventh of nine on debut at Ascot (good to soft; 6-1) last month, but she wasn't beaten far in bunch finish after meeting trouble in steadily run race; no surprise if she improves a fair bit with more luck.

runners.comment: Useful pedigree; yard won last week's Fred Winter at Cheltenham with rare British runner
runners.spotlight: £15,000 3yo; by Getaway out of a bumper and useful 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase winner; that's a plausible pedigree for a race like this, and her stable's only previous runner in Britain this season (Saratoga in last week's Fred Winter) was successful; well worth a market check.

runners.comment: By Jack Hobbs; trainer is a force to be reckoned with (3-10 last five seasons) in bumpers
runners.spotlight: £19,000 3yo; Jack Hobbs half-brother to winners Marie De Medicis (French 1m), Wor Willie (1m4f/1m6f) and Dolly McQueen (1m3f); dam 1m4f winner; trainer has few runners these days but remains a force to be reckoned with (3-10 in last five seasons) in bumpers.

runners.comment: £54,000 3yo; needs keeping an eye on in the market with Alan King running two
runners.spotlight: £54,000 3yo; brother to French 2m1f/2m3f hurdle winner Iban Roque; dam French 1m4f AQPS Flat and 2m3f/2m4f hurdle winner; needs watching in the market with Alan King (16% in bumpers in recent years) running two.

runners.comment: Yard has hit the target six times in bumpers with limited ammunition; interesting on paper
runners.spotlight: E37,000 2yo; No Risk At All half-brother to French 2m hurdle winner Lady Du Chenet; dam maiden jumper, half-sister to useful French 2m1f/2m2f hurdle winner Hotesse Du Chenet; yard has hit the target in bumpers of late with limited ammunition (6-30 in last five seasons); interesting on paper.

runners.comment: Newcomer; stable has well-above-average strike-rate in bumpers; can't be discounted
runners.spotlight: £20,000 3yo; by Passing Glance; brother to bumper/2m3f hurdle winner Glancing Jack; dam 2m-2m4f hurdle winner; stable has maintained a well-above-average strike-rate in bumpers (33%) this season; can't be discounted.

runners.comment: £45,000 3yo; dam useful 1m7f-2m1f hurdle winner; another plausible newcomer
runners.spotlight: £45,000 3yo; by Order Of St George; dam useful 1m7f-2m1f hurdle winner; would have to be useful to make a winning start in a race with plenty of depth, but she's in good hands and it's not impossible.

runners.comment: Bred to be useful; Flat yard does well in bumpers; might be the pick of the newcomers
runners.spotlight: £55,000 3yo; Nathaniel half-sister to 2m4f hurdle winner Blue Run; dam 2m4f hurdle winner, half-sister to useful bumper and 3m/3m1f hurdle winner Lord Generous, out of top-class hurdler Lady Rebecca; bred to be useful and mainly Flat stable has had plenty of bumper winners over the years; could be the pick of the newcomers.

runners.comment: Shaped well when second at Wincanton; gets weight from most; big player for in-form yard
runners.spotlight: Couldn't justify favouritism but still shaped well when second of 14 at Wincanton (good to soft) last month, no extra late on; likely to improve and gets weight from most of her rivals; leading player for in-form yard.

racecards.verdict: Impressive Doncaster winner Diamond Street is feared but in receipt of 21lb the 4yo filly MADAM SPEAKER looks a viable alternative.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Diamond Street, 5/1 Lover Desbois, 6/1 Madam Speaker, 7/1 Bailly's Comet, 8/1 The Mad Poet, 10/1 Keltype, 14/1 Mistral Du Chenet, 16/1 Always Proud,  Sheactslikesummer,  Callisto Queen, 18/1 Irish Goodbye, 22/1 No Way Jay, 25/1 Harzandacassandra,  Master Roque, 33/1 Lady Hope,  Way Maker, 50/1 Show Your Hand,  Bella Decree, 66/1 Spanish Stroll,  Saint Arion

racecards.race_name: John Haine Memorial Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

quotes.race: Betfred Hat Trick Heaven Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We said if Escapeandevade ran the same race as last time, he'd probably win. It's difficult when a horse finishes second lots of times, but he tried his best in both of his races this season and just finished second best. He jumps and gallops and will be better again when he gets deeper ground. There's one of these back here on January 17 and we'll come back for that - Harry Derham, trainer.

quotes.race: Royal Caledonian Hunt Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I think I probably got a little bit lucky. We've had Escapeandevade in the right races and luckily we've had the help of Brian Hughes , because he's a Westerner and he's very awkward. Getting it all right on the day means a lot - James Ewart, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well when second at Worcester on his first run for us last month and jumped really well. He'll run in a handicap chase at Haydock on Betfair Chase day. 19-11-25

runners.breeder: S C P Haras Des Coudraies
runners.comment: Close second over C&D latest; chance on that form but could do with jumping more fluently
runners.spotlight: Almost as good as ever this season and he kept on well when 1l second of four over C&D (good to soft) three weeks ago; a repeat of that form would see him go close, with a tongue-strap added for the first time in Britain, but a losing sequence is developing and he tends to make mistakes.

quotes.race: Howden Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's not very pretty the way Kotmask jumps, but those strides at the last I thought I'd keep going forward on him. I thought we went a good, even gallop. Harry [Cobden] tried to slow it up from the front, but I was quite comfortable turning in and I wanted to keep hold of him as much as I could - Caoilin Quinn, jockey.

quotes.race: Chatteris Fen Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kotmask showed a lot of guts on his third ever start, but he just takes a little bit too long in the air. That'll get ironed out in due course. I wanted a test but I didn't want to make the running, he got a bit lonely in front - Jamie Moore, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I'm sure there's a good race in him this winter, and tracks like Ascot and Sandown suit him well. The softer the ground the better and, while his form has sometimes tailed off as the season has progressed previously, I think he's one to have in your thoughts as this season goes on. He'll come on for his run at Fontwell on Sunday. 28-10-25

He joined us from Gabriel Leenders in November and right from day one he did all we asked. Having won by 12 lengths on his debut for us at Fontwell in December he followed up in the Chatteris Fen Hurdle at Huntingdon, which is always a useful race. We like this horse a lot and he will be entered for the Boodles Hurdle, and if he gets in and the ground is very soft then he will run a big race at a nice price. 02-02-22

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras De La Croix Sonnet Et Al

quotes.race: Century Racing Club Free Horse Giveaway Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Palacio is a big, rangy sort and in time he'll learn to race and be even nicer. He can be a tricky horse at home and the team have done a great job with him - Dylan Johnston, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: It's probably taken a bit of time to work him out, but he has lots of ability and he'll go for the Fulke Walwyn Trophy at Newbury on Friday. If we can keep him in one piece he could be the type for a Grand Annual later in the season. He's always been a big brute of a horse, but as time's gone by he's starting to relax. 23-11-25

He's taken a lot of time to come to himself. He travelled strongly at Exeter on his debut at Exeter in November but then stopped a bit quickly. He's had a wind operation and hopefully we can get him to show us what he can do next time. He'll be out in the next few weeks. 05-01-24

runners.comment: Won first two races over fences but the wheels came off here last time; rebound required
runners.spotlight: Made encouraging start over fences with convincing victory at Windsor (2m, good) on New Year's Day, and he followed up at Haydock (2m, good to soft) two weeks later; however, the wheels came off when he went up in grade for the Greatwood here three weeks ago, and he was beaten before stamina became a factor; 5lb higher than for his second win and needs to get back on track.

quotes.race: Sky Bet, For The Fans Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Koukeo is going the right way and did everything right. They went a good gallop and he saw out the race well and was tough. When he got on better ground up the straight, he jumped better - Jonjo O'Neill, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It was probably all a bit too much for him going over to Punchestown for his first outing in April, but he'd shown some nice pieces of work before finishing second at Chepstow last month. He'll be going over hurdles now and we're keen to get some experience into him. He could be a nice stayer down the line. 06-11-24

runners.owner: G Libson,D Bayliss,T Davies & P Sly
runners.comment: Grand servant; had an excuse when pulled up last time and should be thereabouts
runners.spotlight: Grand servant for the yard with eight wins (six over fences) and he showed he was no back number when second of four at Leicester (2m, soft; handles good) in February; took the wrong course last time; has form here and should be thereabouts.

quotes.race: Boxxe 'Ubique' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Me and Pam [Sly, trainer] thought we'd try cheekpieces for Xcitations. I'm not sure if they had the golden touch or not but they didn't do any harm. He's been a brilliant horse for years now and has won round here a few times. I was always happy, he jumped well and when I went for him he picked up and ran to the line - Paul O'Brien, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Amazing Sri Lanka Elmbridge Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Xcitations loves it around here, but I'm very lucky to have Paul O'Brien, however I'm going to struggle as not only will he be used by Harry Derham but Henrietta Knight will also be using him as he is in there riding out every week. He is great this horse and he has been a star for us. Thankfully he is physically strong enough to carry that sort of weight. Paul said they would go off at some speed and that he would just take his time. He was dropped two pounds for his Kempton run, but I suspect he will now go back up to 140 so I'm not sure where we go after this - Pam Sly, trainer.

quotes.race: Unibet Horserace Betting Operator Of The Year Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jack gave Xcitations a good ride and he's quite a nice horse really. I've always said to the owners that he's going to win them a nice race somewhere. Last season he won twice and then got a fracture in his pedal bone, but he's back now and it all depends on what the handicapper does. We'll just go from handicap to handicap - Pam Sly, trainer.

quotes.race: Each Way Extra At bet365 Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Xcitations never got into a rhythm at Fakenham - it was a disaster from the start. He met the first wrong and everyone wrong after that. He's a lovely jumper, which is one of the main things-Pam Sly, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The most appealing profile belongs to topweight ESCAPEANDEVADE who can bounce back after a break.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Kotmask, 5/2 Escapeandevade, 9/2 Palacio,  Koukeo, 7/1 Xcitations

racecards.race_name: Win Unique Experiences At OLBG Prizes Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Not at his best in 2025 but he's back to his last winning mark and has possibilities
runners.spotlight: Won good-quality handicaps at Aintree (2m5f) and Cheltenham (3m2f) towards end of 2024; not at best in 2025 but he shaped as if retaining ability; missed the Grimthorpe at Doncaster in February due to soft ground; drying conditions should help and, back to his last winning mark, he's a possible.

quotes.race: Sonic The Hedgehog 3 Coming Soon Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: King Turgeon is six and improving. He's put in a career best there, and being by Turgeon, they tend to be slow in coming to hand. My plan was to win the Grand Sefton, so we'll have to go back and have a look now as he's going to rise in the weights. He could be a Grand National horse one day. David Pipe, talking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Grand Sefton Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: From turning in to the line, all King Turgeon has done is keep galloping. He has always been a good jumper, and if he took to these fences that was going to be his asset today. He is a French-bred horse and sometimes they can take a while to adapt and he's still only six so is probably just starting to come into himself and come round to the British way of racing - Jack Tudor, rider.

runners.comment: Well held in two races in the autumn; bit to prove after four months off
runners.spotlight: Veteran; last two wins came in the same 3m2f Cheltenham race in April 2024 and 2025; ran a lacklustre race there in October before possibly failing to stay 3m5f at Ascot; bit to prove after four months off.

quotes.race: Weatherite Air Conditioning Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was important to win for Paddy. Out of his three rides this was the least likely to win but fair play to Sally [Randell, assistant] and people at home because they said Manothepeople was in great form. He was teed up for this. What a way to go out - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Follow Vickers.Bet On Twitter Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You never expect a performance like that first time over fences, but Manofthepeople was very good and got a lovely positive ride. His schooling has been good and he showed a lot of promise last season. He took a while to get going, but Paddy was always sweet on him. We haven't got any plans, but he liked that ground - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

runners.comment: Well held since lengthy break but mark has fallen and he's 2-2 over C&D; quite interesting
runners.spotlight: Has raced only twice since a lengthy layoff, looking rusty on return and seeming not to stay a testing 3m5f at Lingfield two months ago; has to prove he retains all of his ability but his mark is falling, he's still only nine and both his chase successes have come over C&D; quite interesting with Cobden on for the first time this season.

quotes.race: Bet Racing In Running At BetVictor Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (Jacky Upton Trophy) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Welsh National next season will be his target as Makin'yourmindup is a staying chaser who loves testing ground, but I might put him in the Scottish National this season if it were to come up soft or heavy - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Prestige Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Makin'Yourmindup is a lovely horse. I've always thought a lot of him. He's a big horse who just needed a bit of time to grow into himself. He should probably go chasing next year as he jumps his hurdles too well if anything, but today he was tough and galloped all the way to the line - Lorcan Williams, jockey.

quotes.race: Download The Vickers.Bet App Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Makin'youmindup was a big, backward type last term and all he does is gallop and jump so we wanted to make plenty of use of him. It shows how different horses can be for a summer and some time as last season we couldn't really train him - he was such a baby. He'll get further and three miles would suit him well. We were second in the first division of this race with Henri The Second and I might be wrong and doing this horse an injustice, but I'd say Henri is a long way in front of this fella - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's back after a season off. Judged by his two novice chase wins over three miles on heavy ground, he clearly stays well and is suited by testing conditions, so the Welsh National is an obvious target. I'd like to run him first in Chepstow's trial for that race in early December. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Followed Ludlow win with listless effort there; needs headgear to inject some sparkle
runners.spotlight: Rather in and out, and followed a Ludlow win (3m, good to soft) in December with a listless fourth over the same C&D three weeks ago; needs first-time headgear to inject some sparkle.

quotes.race: Tanners Claret Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Sam [Twiston-Davies] gave Ballycamus an absolutely wonderful ride. He was arguably unlucky on his first start of the season at Chepstow, and then he's run in big-field handicaps at Cheltenham. Back to a smaller field here he was a willing partner and probably won with a little in hand - Willy Twiston-Davies, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Not the force of old; poor run in veterans' chase at Doncaster latest; others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Not the force of old and his second at Catterick (3m1f, good) in November came in a two-horse race; followed that with a poor run in a veterans' chase at Doncaster; others appeal more.

quotes.race: Crest Hotels Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Almazhar Garde has been a fantastic horse for us and Paul's always got on really well with him. He'll run through the summer and hopefully he can pick up another win, or two - Charlie Longsdon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He has been very unlucky this season as he's been second in both the Southern and North Yorkshire Nationals, having just been touched off last time over 3m6f. We had been looking at Cheltenham next month, but I think we might leave him this year as he's a long-term Grand National hope. He's in great heart and we're looking at something like the Grimthorpe at Doncaster, or if he missed that the Midlands National would be a nice target. 09-02-22

runners.comment: Younger than most of these and could be unexposed; worth considering in new headgear
runners.spotlight: Younger than most of these and posted a career best when second at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) in February; stiffer task in C&D non-handicap next time; unexposed over this trip and beyond, and drying ground may suit (last win came on good); definitely of interest in first-time headgear.

quotes.race: DragonBet Born From The Betting Ring Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Elysian Knight ran well at Plumpton, his first time over hurdles, I don't think there is massive improvement really. He ran well in his bumpers. We always thought he was a nice horse - Neil Mulholland, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's always been a nice horse and he's done well for a break. He progressed well over hurdles and we think he'll make a decent chaser - he's got it written all over him. quotes.quote: Clarendon House saw it out really well and coasted home. I didn't think it was going anywhere near to plan as he's normally in the front rank. Tom said he gave him a great feel and the pace collapsed a bit in front of him - he timed it perfectly. He's very fast and it'll be the Epsom Dash next and we've unfinished business in that race. Then we might come back here for the Nunthorpe again - he's got something for this track which clearly plays to his assets - Tom Palin, director of operations for Middleham Park Racing, owners.

quotes.race: Build Your Acca With BetUK Handicap
quotes.quote: We didn't quite see that coming into today. It was a massive acid test for Clarendon House and he's passed it with flying colours. We've always had him down as a Listed, borderline Group horse. He ran in a Nunthorpe for us and was put in his place that day, but against these guys he's a horse who is fully effective at five furlongs. The Tapeta seems to suit him and he's put in a monster performance. We've got a serious racehorse that's going to have a big Racing Post Rating in the morning. In terms of the winter season he's a big fish. I think there were 11 higher rated Mehmas' than him in the summer so we thought he not's going to be a stallion, let's do the sensible thing, geld him and see if we can eke out 7lb of improvement, and it looks like that's been proven true. The Listed Hever Sprint (on the track's inaugural Winter Derby card) back at this venue could be on the agenda or we might want to go to slightly sunnier climes. I live in Lincolnshire and Southwell is just south of Lincolnshire, but it'd be lovely to jump on a plane and go to Meydan or somewhere like that for a Group 2. Robert (Cowell, trainer) is virtually imperious when it comes to sprinters and getting the very best out of them, so we're in the very best hands we could possibly be - Tim Palin, owner's director.
