runners.breeder: Messrs A & E Chevalier Du Fau
runners.comment: Takes a big drop in class now after running in a DRF Grade 1, apparent stable selected
runners.spotlight: Scored on debut in a six-runner heavy ground Punchestown bumper last season; well beaten on hurdling debut at Wexford; stayed well a 2m3f Punchestown maiden on soft to heavy; had enough pace to win over 2m1f at Clonmel but should have enough stamina for this; big drop in class now after running in a 2m6f Grade 1 at the DRF.

quotes.race: Munster Hurdle
quotes.quote: Santo Sospir is going the right way, but is still a baby and is learning. Jack said the further he went, the better he got. In fairness, he was gutsy and galloped the whole way to the line. He probably wants two and a half miles but with the conditions, we decided to come here. I'm sure there are races to be won with him and we might look for a rated novice next - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Sebden Steel Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He was good and toughed it out really well from the back of the last. Jack said Santo Sospir lost a bit of momentum when he pricked his ears and ran around a bit at the last. He's obviously stepped forward from Wexford and hopefully he'll be a nice novice going forward. I think further will definitely suit him and he handles those ground conditions, so he'll have loads of options for the winter - Lisa O'Neill, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: He showed a really good attitude to get up late and land a Punchestown bumper in February. He's working well and will return in a maiden hurdle over the coming weeks. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Punchestown maiden winner on second outing over hurdles, a lot more on his plate now
runners.spotlight: Point-to-point winner two years ago for Tom Dreaper; after a lengthy absence, showed promise in a 2m3f maiden at Punchestown in December; duly improved from that run to win over the same course in January; a lot more on his plate now; useful staying prospect.

quotes.race: Matchbook 50:50 Graduation Series Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'd say Shabby Hill will be a nice horse when he steps up to 3m. We bought him in Goresbridge, he had won a point-to-point, and he got a few bits of injuries, that's why he was late coming out. He was maybe over-jumping if anything and I'd say jumping fences will be his forte in time. I don't get carried away with them but I do think he'll make a nice three-mile chaser - Charles Byrnes, trainer

runners.owner: Times Are A Changing Racing Syndicate
runners.comment: C&D maiden winner, third behind an Elliott-trained second-string over at Gowran on latest
runners.spotlight: Point-to-point for Colin Bowe in January 2024; off for almost two years before third in a Limerick bumper in December (2m2f, soft to heavy); built on that to win a C&D maiden hurdle last at 25-1, with a subsequent winner in second; well held in third behind a Gordon Elliott-trained second-string over 2m7f at Gowran.

quotes.race: NavanRacecourse.ie Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He hasn't been in Andy's [Slattery] that long but what we've seen of Timesareachanging we liked. The bumper run was a good one, we were happy coming away from it as the ground was so dead. We were confident of a good run today. He idled away in front, he only gives you what he has to, it was a good performance - Philip Donovan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.comment: Second in a 2m4f bumper last season, two poor runs over hurdles, out of his depth
runners.spotlight: Second in a 2m4f bumper last season; tailed off on hurdling debut at Down Royal; same fate at Naas; out of his depth.

racecards.verdict: Jack Kennedy's mount SANTA SOSPIR, whose sights are lowered after a Grade 1 attempt, is just preferred to Kalypso'schance
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/8 Santo Sospir, 3/1 Timesareachanging, 7/2 Kalypso'chance, 4/1 Shabby Hill, 200/1 Astley

racecards.race_name: Navan Racecourse Maiden Hurdle

runners.comment: No real impression on handicap debut off 105 last time; improvement needed
runners.spotlight: Didn't jump well when tailed off on hurdles debut at Thurles (2m4f, good to yielding); better next time when a 28l fifth at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yielding); 21l behind in fifth at Thurles in February; no real impression when beaten 12.5l on handicap debut at Leopardstown last time off 105 (2m3f, soft to heavy); improvement needed.

racecards.verdict: At worst, FLY AWAY HOME would have been third but for unseating at the final flight at Leopardstown last time, and she can make amends
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Haveanothertry, 3/1 Fly Away Home, 100/30 Champagne Venture, 8/1 Sticktothescript, 13/1 Better Times,  Lord Tobin, 15/1 The Shanty Field, 18/1 Gallant George, 33/1 Beau Della

racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Handicap Chase Final (Listed Race)

runners.breeder: M Francois Xavier Chaussonniere & Mme Doina Chaussonniere
runners.comment: On course for three-timer; beat Maxi Mac Gold and Nelson County latest; hvy ground ideal
runners.spotlight: On course for a three-timer following a 22l win at Navan (second won easily next time) and victory in a Fairyhouse novice chase last time (3m2f, heavy) with 1l back to Maxi Mac Gold and 4.75l to Nelson County; won't want to see the ground dry out too much but not ruled out.

quotes.race: William Hill Each Way Extra Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: He jumped brilliant and loves that heavy ground. Rokathir is lightly raced and needs this sort of ground - Darragh O'Keeffe, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Book Your Group Deal Today Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rokathir travelled and jumped great. He fell the last day here (over fences) when I still though I had half a a chance and the winner went on and won again at Fairyhouse. He had a nice weight and coped with the ground well. He was a bit quirky when he first came but the penny is beginning to drop now. Darragh O'Keefe, jockey talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Third at Punchestown before UR at final flight last time when possible winner; chance
runners.spotlight: No wins since two hurdles two seasons ago at around 2m4f; much improved to take third in the Punchestown Grand National Trial in February (3m4f, heavy), coming from further back than first two; may have won a Listed contest at Naas last time (3m1f, soft to heavy) but unseated at the last when jumping into challenger; he's in form and no surprise to see him feature.

quotes.race: Punchestown Members Club From 215 Euros Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was delighted when I saw we were going to get Limerick ground again. Built By Ballymore just handles the muck so well. He might not quicken up in it but he keeps going in it. I thought his rating was high enough, but he just handles that ground better than most - Martin Brassil, trainer.

quotes.race: CUBE Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Built By Ballymore is a big raw horse and will take a while to come to himself. I was happy enough where I was sitting, I kicked on two out and he will have learned loads from that - Conor Brassil, rider.

runners.comment: Easy winner over fences and then hurdles last time; up 10lb compared to win but big chance
runners.spotlight: 2m5f maiden hurdle winner ran well upped to 3m for his handicap chase debut here when third (3m, soft to heavy); built on that to comfortably score at Punchestown (2m7f, soft to heavy) and took advantage of his lower hurdles mark here last time, winning by 4l (2m4f, heavy); he's 10lb higher than his Punchestown win but is towards the top of the shortlist.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Extra Places Amateur National (Q.R.) Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Derek was very good. He does it time and time again, he's top class. Today was kind of the plan and we'll take it from here. We'll have a chat with Frank [Berry] and see what he says to the boss and go from there. I think Showurappreciation can go further as he jumps well and is a staying chaser. He jumped very, very well for a big horse. You'd be delighted with him. You wouldn't be running him on very quick ground - Jonathan Sweeney, trainer.

runners.comment: 14l winner of novice chase weakened into third over 3m2f last time; this trip looks right
runners.spotlight: Cork handicap hurdle winner (3m1f, soft) built upon a decent chasing debut to win a Fairyhouse novice chase by 14l next time (2m6f, yielding); looked bred to stay 3m2f trip in a Fairyhouse novice chase last time but weakened into third behind Rokathir and Maxi Mac Gold; based on that, drop to this trip seems the right move, and it's still early day over fences; interesting.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Nelson County is a nice horse with a very good pedigree. He won last year on soft ground over three miles at Cork and was always going to be a chaser. This trip is as short as he wants and he won as he liked. We had him in at Down Royal on New Year's Day but we were worried about the ground being a bit dry. He definitely grabs at the ground so we sidestepped to come here. He's not flashy at home but the further he goes, the better he gets - Ross O'Sullivan, trainer.

runners.comment: Winner of h'cap chase debut but never travelling last time; needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Point/hurdle/bumper winner was beaten favourite in two beginners' chases before making immediate impact on handicap chase debut at Leopardstown (3m1f, yielding); raised 6lb for that but was never travelling in a Naas Listed event last time (2m4f, heavy); needs to bounce back.

stable_tour.quote: You'd have to say he was a bit disappointing at Galway on Saturday. We think he's better than that and we will look for a similar sort of maiden hurdle for him next time. 28-10-24

runners.comment: A mistake at the last may have cost her on h'cap chase debut last time; thereabouts
runners.spotlight: Punchestown maiden hurdle winner was a distant second in the third of her beginners' chase starts at Naas (2m4f, soft); improved for switch to handicaps in a Listed contest back there last time (2m4f, heavy) when making a mistake at the last and being headed in the final strides; up 6lb for that but should be thereabouts.

quotes.race: Get Your Punchestown Festival 2025 Tickets Today Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Magic McColgan just got progressively worse in hanging and jumping left. They went a good gallop and she appreciated the step up in trip and slow ground. She is a fine mare and has a good jump in her - Paul Townend, rider.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares' INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: That was a very nice performance. It was a nice step forward from Magic Mccolgan's run at Christmas and I imagine she'll go on to Punchestown now for the Listed mares' bumper, unless there's one in the meantime, but I think that is the plan - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A nice filly by Flemensfirth who we're looking forward to getting to the track. 13-11-23

runners.comment: H'cap chase winner was close off new mark next time; tongue tie on after tailed off latest
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdles winner came good over fences on handicap bow at Clonmel in a novice contest last month (2m2f, heavy) and only narrowly denied off 9lb higher here next time (2m5f, soft to heavy); tongue tie on now after tailed off effort at Naas last time; in the mix if giving his best.

quotes.race: Next Race Meeting January 8th Novice Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: It's nice to get the yard a winner again. There are plenty talking about the form of them. It's just one of those things. There are plenty of good horses, so it will get going again. That's probably why we couldn't be fully confident in Bridie's Beau coming today. He had a good run the last day, the race just didn't suit him, they went slow. The deeper ground suited him today and it was good to get his head in front - Keith Donoghue, rider.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Triple Crown Series At Punchestown Festival 2025 Qualifier Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Bridie's Beau has taken a step forward and travelled brilliantly. He was gutsy too. He met the second-last on a wrong stride and lost a bit of momentum but he was brave. He has enough size and scope about him to keep improving. For the money that's on offer at the final of this race, you'd certainly have to consider going for it - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

runners.owner: Mrs K Browne & Mrs Anne Coffey
runners.comment: Jumped left when runner-up behind Rokathir last time, Nelson County in third; chance
runners.spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner ran well in a Naas handicap hurdle in February last year off 124 (2m7f, heavy); didn't set the world alight in beginners' chase starts, but much better in a novice chase at Fairyhouse last time (3m2f, heavy); kept on well to take the runner-up spot, 1l behind Rokathir with 3.75l back to Nelson County; jumped left throughout that day so this track can help, however slightly worse off at the weights now.

quotes.race: Racing Again May 21st Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Maxi Mac Gold was the horse I fancied today. He is very genuine and he rides a classy sort of horse. His winter form was a class above any of these - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

runners.comment: Rated 18lb higher over hurdles; 0-7 over fences; took third last time but others preferred
runners.spotlight: 0-7 over fences with an 18lb lower mark in this sphere; easily won a Listed hurdle here in December (3m2f, soft to heavy); fell back over fences at Punchestown next time before making a couple of jumping errors when a beaten 5-2 favourite over 3m here in February (heavy); stayed on for third at Leopardstown last time (3m5f, yielding to soft).

quotes.race: St. Peter's Dunboyne GAA Maiden Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: Gringo D'Aubrelle is a nice horse that probably wants 2m4f. I love the way he put his head down and battled the whole way up the straight - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: This chap is well handicapped. I think he's better than a 115-rated chaser for sure. He hasn't been easy to train but when he puts it all together there's a day in him. 26-10-25

quotes.race: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Sammy Smart loves Punchestown and ran really well in Thurles a couple of weeks ago. He tends to need a good gap between his races. I thought this might be on the short side, but it worked out grand and James [Smith] was very strong on him. I couldn't get a good look at it but he told me he halved a few fences going around, which never helps - Thomas Gibney, trainer.

runners.comment: 5-13 in points and opened track account at 18th attempt in Jan'; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Record of 5-13 in points; opened account on the track at the 18th attempt, improving on hunter chase form to land a 2m5f handicap at Fairyhouse off 104 in January (soft); maintained consistency with a promoted third at Thurles last time (2m2f, soft); others preferred.

racecards.verdict: Many appealing options. NELSON COUNTY gets the vote, but this is tricky and fascinating in equal measure and a lot deserve a close look

racecards.race_name: Kilberry Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Chase winner over Christmas; okay efforts over hurdles/fences since but others preferred
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdles winner got off the mark over fences at Limerick over Christmas in a novice contest (2m2f, soft to heavy); solid second over hurdles at Naas following that but poor next time; returned to fences at Gowran last time when weakened into an 8.25l fifth (2m, heavy); others preferred.

quotes.race: O'Kelly Brothers Demolition Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Moudan is improving the whole time. Obviously, it mightn't have gone to plan the first couple of days, but we don't mind now. He wasn't doing a whole lot the whole way. When they came to me, he started to wake up and concentrate on his job and he was good when I needed him at the last - Eoin Walsh, jockey.

runners.comment: Mixed form in all spheres since adding second chase win in March last year
runners.spotlight: Flat and hurdles winner scored twice in succession over fences at Thurles in March last year over 2m5f on good/good to yielding ground; mixed form in all spheres since, pulled up at Limerick in October when last seen (2m3f, yielding to soft); remains 5lb above last winning mark.

quotes.race: Junction 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Spinning Web has been woken up by hurdles and he adapted quickly at home. Hopefully that will make him brave enough to win over further on the Flat - Danny Mullins, rider.

runners.comment: Shaped well on h'cap debut last time; Mark Walsh rides for the first time; good chance
runners.spotlight: One of two for trainer; McManus homebred was well-backed to win a maiden hurdle at the fifth attempt at Kilbeggan in April; well beaten in two high-quality beginners' chases this season, but shaped well on handicap debut at Naas (2m, soft) last time, disputing for second before weakening into third; Mark Walsh rides for the first time now; good chance.

runners.comment: Point/dual hurdles winner; poor in beginners' but h'cap chase debut now with Donoghue up
runners.spotlight: One of two for trainer; point-to-point winner added his second hurdles win at Listowel in June off 116 (2m, good); poor form shown in three recent beginners' chases but this is his first handicap chase and the fact Donoghue chooses him over Kazakh d'Arthel looks significant.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV With A Free Trial Now Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was kind of happy enough that they had gone a good gallop early on and I was happy enough to give them a little bit of rope heading down the back straight to get a little breather in and I finished off well because of that. Stuntman Steve's form is consistent, I had only ridden him once beforehand but it was over a longer trip and he rides like he wants a little bit further but then I don't know if he stays it so he is a little bit in between. A strongly run race probably suits him - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: The final hurdle was the winning of the race for Stuntman Steve and thankfully he came up for me. We have him six weeks and while he hadn't been away, we thought he was a nice horse so thought he'd go close - Keith Donoghue, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He had more letters than numbers in his point-to-point form but he's a grand horse. He won at Ballingarry in May and then made a winning start for us in a maiden hurdle at Clonmel last week when the front two pulled 17 lengths clear. I'm not sure where we go from here but he's qualified for the auction final at Punchestown. I suppose a rated novice could be next for him. 12-11-24

He's a grand horse who won his maiden hurdle at Clonmel last week and the front two pulled 17 lengths clear. He's qualified for the auction final at Punchestown and I suppose a rated novice could be next. 13-11-24

runners.owner: Call It What You Like Syndicate
runners.comment: Moderate form shown in last two hurdle runs; would appreciate better ground
runners.spotlight: Dual AW winner has a win apiece over hurdles and fences; moderate form shown in last two runs over hurdles, finishing eighth both times; returns to chasing now and he will appreciate better ground if it appears; others preferred.

quotes.race: Willwego.com Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I thought Someone's Wish would come on for the run. Jack [Kennedy, jockey] said they went very fast up front and it played into his hands. He held onto him as long as he could and said he'd come on plenty from it - Gordon Elliott, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: It was nice to see him get his head back in front at Downpatrick and we've him pencilled in for the 2m handicap chase at Down Royal this week. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Poor in beginners' and just modest improvement for switch to a h'cap last time
runners.spotlight: One of two for trainer; poor in opening beginners' chases and just modest improvement for switch to a handicap last time when beaten 21l; trainer's/owner's best chance appears to be Park That.

runners.comment: 0-10 chasing but good runs in defeat; Mark Walsh rides Park That
runners.spotlight: Winning hurdler; 0-10 chasing but rated 4lb superior in this discipline after runner-up finishes at Punchestown (2m4f, yielding to soft) and Naas (2m4f, heavy); finished 16l behind in a Naas Listed contest when sporting first-time cheekpieces (left off now), in a race won by another McManus runner ridden by Mark Walsh; similarly Walsh rides Park That here.

runners.comment: 0-8 over fences but running well and placed on several occasions; wants dry ground
runners.spotlight: 0-8 over fences, but has been running well; placed on several occasions, including at Thurles in November when last seen, keeping on for an 11.5l third (2m6f, good to yielding); will want the ground to continue to dry.

runners.comment: Makes chasing debut from 13lb outside the handicap; hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Not beaten far on handicap debut over hurdles in January but lesser efforts have followed; makes chasing debut now from 13lb outside the handicap proper; hard to fancy.

racecards.verdict: Shaping nicely on handicap debut last time, PARK THAT will now have Mark Walsh aboard for the first time and appeals most

runners.owner: J J Leckey & Donal P Keane & P J Rothwell
runners.comment: Half-brother to French 2m2f hurdle winner Mon Getaway; best watched unless market speaks
runners.spotlight: 8,000GBP yearling and bought for 11,000euros as 3yo; second foal; half-brother to French 2m2f hurdle winner Mon Getaway; dam maiden hurdler stayed 2m4f, sister to bumper/2m-3m2f hurdle winner Jersey Lady, half-sister to Irish National winner Burrows Saint; best watched unless market speaks.

runners.comment: Half-brother to two winners inc' The Doyen Chief (RPR 144); others more likely
runners.spotlight: Purchased for 18,000euros as a 3yo; sixth foal; half-brother to winners The Doyen Chief (useful bumper and 2m3f-3m hurdle/chase) and Arctic Angel (3m2f hurdle); dam unraced half-sister to 2m4f-2m6f hurdle winner Cooksgrove Lady (dam of high-class chaser Castlebawn West); others more likely.

runners.comment: Half-brother to bumper/3m2f hurdle winner Jem In Em; check market.
runners.spotlight: Sixth foal; half-brother to bumper/3m2f hurdle winner Jem In Em; dam well beaten in bumper, half-sister to smart 2m1f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Long House Hall and useful 2m7f chase winner Willyanwoody; check market.

runners.comment: Dromahane point winner in Dec'; form of that race looks moderate but won by 5l
runners.spotlight: 34,000euros foal, purchased for 30,000euros as a 3yo; brother to point/2m4f hurdle winner Kalkbrenner; dam pulled up in point only start, sister to useful bumper/2m hurdle winner Quick Grabim, half-sister to useful 2m4f/2m5f chase winner Having A Cut; won a Dromahane point by 5l for Jonathan Fogarty in December, but form of the race looks moderate.

runners.comment: Half-sister to bumper winners Shantou's Melody and Glens Lullaby; of obvious interest
runners.spotlight: Harzand filly; half-sister to bumper winners Shantou's Melody and Glens Lullaby; dam smart bumper and 2m2f-2m6f hurdle winner, sister to bumper/2m hurdle winner Glens Harmony, closely related to useful 2m-3m hurdle winner Lean Araig; of obvious interest.

runners.comment: Dam placed 2m2f-3m hurdles; hooded for debut and best watched.
runners.spotlight: Third foal; dam placed 2m2f-3m hurdles, closely related to 2m-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Could Be Trouble, out of unraced sister to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Looks Like Trouble; hooded for debut and best watched.

runners.comment: Half-brother to three winners inc' Shoot First (RPR 146); tongue ti on for debut
runners.spotlight: Cost 13,000euros as a foal; half-brother to winners Shoot First (useful 2m4f/3m hurdle), Spin A Yarn (2m1f hurdle) and Neon Dream (point); dam unraced half-sister to smart 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase winner Watson Lake; tongue tie on for debut.

runners.comment: Harzand filly; sister to point winner Lets Go Harry; best watched unless strong in market
runners.spotlight: Harzand filly; sister to point winner Lets Go Harry; unraced dam closely related to useful winners A Great View (2m-3m1f hurdle/chase) and Roll It Out (2m hurdle), out of unraced half-sister to smart bumper/2m-2m4f hurdle winner Liss A Paoraigh; best watched unless strong in market.
